title: Special Investigations Investigator, Consultant
description:
Your Role

The Special Investigations Unit (SIU) team s responsible for preventing, detecting, investigating, and resolving health care fraud, waste, and abuse. The Special Investigations Investigator, Consultant report to the SIU manager. In this role you will conduct investigations in accordance with company policies and procedures and in compliance with all applicable laws and regulations; for all lines of business. This role requires travel to provider locations to conduct onsite provider audits, as needed.


Your Work

In this role, you will:

  • Serve as a senior subject matter expert handling the most complex and sensitive investigations
  • Provide expert guidance, mentoring, and quality review for investigators, ensuring consistency, defensibility, and audit readiness
  • Establish and maintain investigative standards, tools, templates, and training resources to improve team effectiveness
  • Partner strategically with law enforcement, regulators, and internal leadership to support high risk or high impact cases
  • Apply expert discretion to ensure investigations align with legal, regulatory, and policy requirements
  • Conduct medical record audits
  • Travel to provider locations to conduct onsite audits
  • Initiate, analyze, develop and successfully complete complex fraud investigations and communicate investigation and audit findings with limited to no supervisory assistance
  • Be responsible for coordinating and overseeing efforts to recover erroneous payments made because of a claims processing error, misrepresentative billing, fraud, abuse, or any other criminal act with no assistance
  • Document all stages of each investigation using company and department procedures, templates and form. Prepare detailed post audit investigative reports. Limited to no supervisory assistance needed

Your Knowledge and Experience

  • Bachelor’s degree or High School Diploma/GED and 4 years of additional relevant experience in lieu of a degree
  • Requires 7 years of prior relevant experience related to fraud, waste, and abuse
  • Requires excellent presentation/interpersonal/negotiation skills
  • Requires proficiency in MS Office and data mining tools
  • Requires extensive experience in health care, compliance, privacy, legal services, and or investigations
  • Requires deep knowledge of reimbursement/program(s)
  • Requires extensive experience of claim review and coding knowledge
  • Requires extensive knowledge in auditing medical documentation to substantiate services billed on a claim(s)
  • Requires excellent analytical and thinking skills
  • Requires excellent written and verbal communication and negotiation without guidance

Hybrid

This role requires employees to be in-office based on our hybrid workplace model, balancing purposeful in-person collaboration with flexibility. For most teams, this means coming into the office two days each week.

Employees living more than 50 miles from an office location will work with their manager to determine in-office time based on business need.

title: DEPARTMENT CLERK 3 CAA
description:
This position requires frequent daily communication and coordination with probation officers, clerical staff, supervisors, law enforcement agencies, Children & Youth Services, the District Attorney's Office, Victim/Witness Services, court personnel, and other agencies involved in the juvenile justice system.

The Departmental Clerk III utilizes multiple information systems and software applications to maintain accurate juvenile records, process court-related information, prepare reports, manage documentation, and support the operational needs of the Juvenile Probation Office. The employee works under the direction of the Programming

and Development Supervisor and performs other related duties as assigned.

Essential Functions and Responsibilities

  • Maintains an electronic log of police reports received by the Juvenile Probation Office and enters applicable reports into JCMS and CPCMS.
  • Assigns file numbers to all new and existing juvenile files when new charges are received.
  • Prepares, completes, and distributes various reports, including the daily detention list and weekly warrant list, for use by probation staff.
  • Enters detention, demographic, program, and charge information into applicable computer systems for juveniles who have been arrested.
  • Enters and processes information accurately and in a timely manner in accordance with established procedures.
  • Uploads, scans, and maintains hard-copy and electronic documents in OnBase.
  • Completes and processes outcome court orders in CPCMS following juvenile court hearings.
  • Reviews and processes delinquency petition information for accuracy and completeness.
  • Enters court dispositions into JCMS and CPCMS.
  • Updates juvenile contact and demographic information in JCMS and CPCMS as changes are received.
  • Establishes and maintains effective working relationships with individuals, law enforcement personnel, court personnel, and agencies involved in the development and ongoing operation of the office's Management Information Systems.
  • Develops and maintains proficiency in applicable software programs and computer systems, including Microsoft Word, spreadsheets, database applications, JCMS, CPCMS, and CLEAN.
  • Downloads and enters juvenile photographs into JCMS in accordance with established procedures.
  • Retrieves and reviews information in CPCMS, JCMS, CLEAN, and other applicable systems as needed; enters warrants and performs related system functions.
  • Updates detention, placement, and community-based program information in JCMS and ensures appropriate information is transmitted to Children & Youth Services business staff.
  • Schedules detention hearings and hearings for services on the court calendar in CPCMS.
  • Assists with entering vehicle-related information into FLEETIO.
  • Enters police reports for detained and non-detained juveniles into JCMS and CPCMS and electronically scans and forwards applicable reports for detained cases to the District Attorney's Office and Victim/Witness Services.
  • Runs the petition report each Friday and distributes it to the District Attorney's Office to identify missing petitions.
  • Reviews and corrects the monthly JCMS error report to ensure data accuracy and integrity.
  • Enters revocations and motions into CPCMS.
  • Monitors and maintains the juvenile allegation email inbox and processes information received through the inbox in accordance with established procedures.
  • Provides assistance with telephone coverage as needed.
  • Provides coverage for the juvenile court run and distribution of court orders in the absence of the Departmental Clerk II.
  • Assists with other clerical, administrative, data-entry, and office-related duties as assigned.

Required Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

The successful candidate must demonstrate the following knowledge, skills, and abilities:

  • Ability to accurately enter, retrieve, update, and maintain information in computerized databases and information systems.
  • Strong knowledge of English language, spelling, grammar, punctuation, and standard usage.
  • Working knowledge of court processes and procedures applicable to the Juvenile Probation Office.
  • Ability to perform detailed, repetitive work accurately and efficiently with minimal supervision.
  • Ability to maintain strict confidentiality of juvenile, court, law enforcement, and other sensitive information in accordance with applicable laws, policies, procedures, and supervisory direction.
  • Ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships with supervisors, coworkers, professional staff, probation personnel, law enforcement officers, court personnel, outside agencies, and other individuals.
  • Working knowledge of Microsoft Office applications and the ability to become proficient in JCMS, CPCMS, CLEAN, OnBase, FLEETIO, and other applicable systems.
  • Skill in operating standard office equipment, including computers, telephones, scanners, photocopiers, and related equipment.
  • Ability to communicate clearly, professionally, and effectively, both verbally and in writing.
  • Ability to understand and accurately carry out oral and written instructions.
  • Ability to prioritize and organize multiple assignments while meeting established deadlines.
  • Ability to learn and perform the essential duties of related clerical positions to provide operational coverage when coworkers are absent or unavailable.
  • Ability to exercise sound judgment, maintain attention to detail, and identify and correct discrepancies in data and documentation.

Minimum Training and Experience

Graduation from an accredited high school or completion of an approved equivalency program. Post-secondary education, vocational or trade school training, and/or coursework in secretarial science, office administration, computer operations, information systems, or a related field is preferred. Relevant clerical, administrative, data-entry, court, or computer systems experience is desirable.

An equivalent combination of education, training, and experience may be considered.

Additional Requirements

Employment in this position is contingent upon:

  • Possession of a valid driver's license and a satisfactory driving record.
  • Successful completion of a criminal background check.
  • Successful completion of required Pennsylvania child abuse clearances.
  • Successful completion of required FBI clearances.
  • Ability to maintain confidentiality and comply with all applicable County, Juvenile Probation Office, court, and legal requirements governing the handling of juvenile and other protected information.

Position Responsibilities

The Departmental Clerk III is expected to perform assigned responsibilities accurately, efficiently, professionally, and in accordance with established policies and procedures. Because the position supports multiple functions within the Juvenile Probation Office, flexibility, dependability, attention to detail, and the ability to assume related duties when necessary are essential to the successful performance of this position.

title: Emergency Services Technician (ER Tech)
location: Lake Havasu City, AZ, United States
description:
Emergency Services Technician (ER Tech)

Job Type: PRN | Varied

Schedule: 12/hr. shifts, Varied (1-3 days per week)

Your experience matters

Havasu Regional Medical Center is part of Lifepoint Health, a diversified healthcare delivery network with facilities coast to coast. We are driven by a profound commitment to prioritize your well-being so you can provide exceptional care to others. As an Emergency Services Technician (ER Tech) joining our team, you're embracing a vital mission dedicated to making communities healthier ®. Join us on this meaningful journey where your skills, compassion and dedication will make a remarkable difference in the lives of those we serve.

More about our team

At Havasu Regional Medical Center's Emergency Department, our team is built on collaboration, trust, and a shared commitment to delivering exceptional emergency care. As a Paramedic, you'll have the unique opportunity to expand your clinical expertise by gaining valuable hospital-based emergency medicine experience that strengthens your prehospital skills. Our team embraces a true "no one works alone" culture, with coworkers and physicians who are approachable, supportive, and always willing to help one another. Leadership maintains an open-door policy, creating an environment where every team member feels valued, supported, and empowered to grow. From caring for high-acuity trauma and emergency patients to participating in process improvement and professional development opportunities, you'll be part of a close-knit team that works together to make a difference for our patients and our community both inside and outside the hospital.

How you’ll contribute

An Emergency Services Technician (ER Tech) who excels in this role:

  • Greets patients and visitors. Answers, screens, and routes telephone calls. Calls codes, pages, and overhead announcements as requested.
  • Enters nursing requests subject to the approval of a licensed nurse. Asks for clarification when necessary.
  • Assists with processing patient admissions, transfers and discharges. Assembles and maintains patient records and charts.
  • Performs needed clerical tasks, including copying, filing, and ordering/stocking supplies.
  • Assists RNs and physicians with other patient activities as needed.
  • Performs continual surveillance of multiple monitors.
  • Identifies significant arrhythmias and/or signs of patient distress and intervenes appropriately. Identifies and corrects for artifacts.
  • Reports abnormal assessment and telemetry findings or changes in patient physical, mental, and emotional conditions to nursing staff.
  • Tests equipment for proper working order. Reports equipment problems to supervisor.

Why join us

We believe that investing in our employees is the first step to providing excellent patient care. In addition to your base compensation, this position also offers:

  • Comprehensive Benefits: Multiple levels of medical, dental and vision coverage for full-time and part-time employees.
  • Financial Protection & PTO: Life, accident, critical illness, hospital indemnity insurance, short- and long-term disability, paid family leave and paid time off.
  • Financial & Career Growth: Higher education and certification tuition assistance, loan assistance and 401(k) retirement package and company match.
  • Employee Well-being: Mental, physical, and financial wellness programs (free gym memberships, virtual care appointments, mental health services and discount programs).
  • Professional Development: Ongoing learning and career advancement opportunities.

What we're looking for

An applicant who has successfully completed Graduated from an approved EMT Paramedic or EMT Intermediate program.

Additional requirements include:

  • Certifications: Basic Life Support (BLS) within 30 days of hire;
  • Required Skills: Requires critical thinking skills, decisive judgment and the ability to work with minimal supervision. Must be able to work in a stressful environment and take appropriate action.
  • Licenses: Certified Nursing Aide license is preferred.
  • Education: High school diploma or equivalent is required.
    Graduated from an approved EMT Paramedic or EMT Intermediate program.
  • Experience: Minimum 1 year of experience.

More about Havasu Regional Medical Center

Havasu Regional Medical Center is a Joint Commission accredited, Medicare certified hospital located in Lake Havasu City, Arizona. Havasu Regional Medical Center is a joint venture between PHC-Lake Havasu, Inc. and many community physicians. Through this ongoing collaboration, we are able to identify and focus on the elements that make for a

quality-driven healthcare environment for our patients. Havasu Regional Medical Center is partially owned or invested in by physicians.

As a community hospital and regional referral center for healthcare, Havasu Regional Medical Center offers a broad and comprehensive scope of services in major medical disciplines. A medical staff of more than 33 affiliated physicians represents a broad cross section of expertise in 31 medical specialties.

Havasu Regional Medical Center provides 24-hour emergency service with full-time emergency physicians on duty. title: Principal Piping Engineer
description:
Job Overview:

The Principal Piping Engineer is responsible for interpreting internal or external business issues and recommending best practices. They will be tasked with solving complex Piping-related problems and will work independently with minimal guidance. The Principal Piping Engineer may be responsible for leading functional teams or projects and is regarded as a specialist in the field of Piping. As such, they must have in-depth expertise in Piping as well as broad knowledge of the Piping discipline within the Engineering function.

Key Task and Responsibilities:

  • Perform conceptual, FEED, or detailed design analysis and develop them as per project Scope of Work design basis, project documentation, design codes and standards, and McDermott procedures within the planned schedule and budget
  • Apply in-depth skills and broad knowledge of the business to address complex problems and non-standard situations and report them to the Project Management Team and Department Manager at an early stage
  • Prepare detailed design calculations and analyses including design reports and procedures
  • Manage own time to meet objectives and forecast and plan resource requirements
  • Lead others to solve complex problems, use sophisticated analytical thought to exercise judgment, and identify innovative solutions
  • Interpret internal/external business challenges and recommend best practices to improve technology, processes, or services
  • Explain difficult concepts and negotiate with others to adopt a different point of view
  • Focused on health and safety policies and procedures
  • When acting as Lead engineer:
    • Direct medium or large Engineering and Design team as a Lead Engineer
    • Lead the Discipline engineering design of the assigned work area and complete within the planned schedule and budget, in accordance with standards, MDR, and project-specific procedures and to a high professional standard
    • Plan, organize, and direct all aspects of discipline execution of the assigned project including scope, deliverables, schedule, and manpower resources
    • Ensure interfaces and deliverables are clearly identified
    • Maintain responsibility for progress and productivity, identifying any required corrective action
    • Act as project representative for the discipline during meetings with the project team, Client, and relevant agencies such as certifying authorities, auditors, third parties, etc.
  • Become fully familiar with the project SoW, Specification, Schedule, and all inter-discipline requirements
  • Interface with other departments to obtain input for engineering and design
  • Interface with High-Value Centers (HVECs) ensuring a clear understanding of their SoW
  • Prepare Iso Curve based on required input in line with Project Level 3 Schedule
  • When acting as Lead Engineer or area Lead:
    • Review the Piping budget, and provide Piping input for the Project Execution Plan
    • Plan, organize, and assign tasks, responsibilities, and man-hour budgets to piping sub-discipline and verify tasks are completed within budgets
    • Support 3D-Model review at 30%, 60% & 90% progress
    • Provide Piping Discipline input into Plan Level 2, 3, and 4 schedules and review the dependencies
    • Prepare discipline forecasts identifying changes to scope and promptly raising a notification
    • Alert the team of any deviation from the Scope of work or a need for a change order
    • Provide piping man-hours, schedule, and deliverables list including Piping Discipline Execution Plan
    • Check and approve design philosophies, specifications, pipe supports, standard detail drawings, MTO, and material requisitions in accordance with the project scope of work and contract
    • Monitor KPI measurement results and take corrective action
    • Lead Piping Discipline during project internal or External Audits
  • Assist the Department Manager in the Performance Evaluation of Piping team members
  • Support proposals and studies

Reports to:
Project: Lead Engineer, Project Engineer or Project Manager
Functional: Department Manager
Liaise With: Designers and Engineers, other Engineering disciplines Leads, Construction & Fabrication Group,
Project Management Team, Document Control, Project Cost Control and Planning Group, Procurement Group,
Subcontractors and Vendors, Client
Supervises: Piping Engineering and Layout Team

Essential Qualification and Education:

  • Bachelor's Degree or Master's Degree in Mechanical Engineering
  • 15-20 years of experience as a Piping Engineer in Oil and gas with a major contractor performing Conceptual, Pre-FEED, FEED, and detail design
  • Previous experience as Lead Piping Engineer on FEED and EPC projects via Multi-offices Project Execution
  • Detailed knowledge of Pre-FEED, FEED, and Detailed Design Phases Projects
  • Detailed knowledge and experience of design techniques and application of standards, codes, and guidelines
  • Familiar with all Piping Sub-Disciplines including Design and Modelling, Pipe Stress & Support, Piping Material Engineering, and MTO activities and deliverables
  • Knowledgeable in project coordination and execution skills
  • Conversant with international codes and standards like ANSI, ASME, API, BS, NFPA, etc.
  • Familiar with SP3D / E3D / Navisworks
  • Familiar with stick-built and modularization approach
  • Preferably Registered Professional Engineer or member of a professional engineering society
  • Familiar with commercial aspects of projects and types of contracts
  • Committed to McDermott values
  • Flexible for Business travel

title: Postbud, Timelønnede vikarer på Oppdal, Støren og Røros
description:
Er du glad i å kjøre bil og ønsker å jobbe som postbud?

Vi søker timelønnede vikarer (tilkalling ved behov) på Oppdal, Støren og Røros

Som postbud hos oss er du en viktig ambassadør for Posten Bring AS i møte med kundene. Den vi ser etter er serviceinnstilt, selvgående og til å stole på. Du liker en hektisk hverdag med varierte oppgaver der kundens behov står i fokus. Stillingen inngår i et team som jobber etter Posten Bring sine verdier, Tar ansvar, Spiller på lag og Vil mer. Arbeidstiden er i h.h.t lokal arbeidstidsplan.

Stillingene har for tiden oppmøtested på Oppdal, Støren og Røros

Arbeidsoppgaver:

  • Utkjøring av pakker, brev og øvrige Posten Bring produkter til våre kunder
  • Henting av brev og pakker i postkasse
  • Lasting av bil til utkjøring/innhenting
  • Kontakt med kunder
  • Vedlikehold og klargjøring av utstyr
  • Ivareta Postens biler og utstyr på en god måte

Hvem vi ser etter:

  • Førerkort klasse B
  • Gode norskkunnskaper både muntlig og skriftlig
  • Jobben kan være fysisk krevende, og det er stor fordel å være i god form
  • Det er fordel om du liker å jobbe strukturert, selv om dagene kan være forskjellige
  • Forståelse for digitale verktøy og evnen til å håndtere disse

Hva kan du forvente av en dag som postbud
Å være postbud handler om mer enn bare å levere post – det er en hverdag fylt med frisk luft og mye aktivitet. Hver dag er preget av rutiner, men ingen dag er lik. Våre postbud verdsetter en aktiv hverdag med frihet, ansvar og evnen til å håndtere det uventede. Jobben som postbud gir deg en meningsfull og dynamisk arbeidshverdag.

Dagen starter på terminalen hvor du forbereder dagens rute sammen med kollegene dine. Du har ansvar for å levere brev, pakker, og reklame til våre kunder på en rute, men det er forventet at du jobber sammen og hjelper dine kolleger ved behov. Dette er noe for deg som liker selvstendighet, men du må også være forberedt på varierte dager, spesielt når snøen laver ned eller pakkehaugene vokser.

Som postbud er du Postens ansikt utad. Det er en fordel at du syns arbeidsoppgavene er interessante og utfører de med ansvarlighet, slik at våre kunder får et godt inntrykk av oss.

Hvorfor velge Posten?
Hos oss får du mulighet til å jobbe i et av Norges mest innovative selskaper. Selv om rollen som postbud på mange måter er tradisjonell, bruker vi moderne kjøretøy, teknologi og digitale verktøy.

Vi har et trivelig arbeidsmiljø med godt samhold og fellesskap, samt gode lønnsbetingelser og pensjons- og forsikringsordninger.

Kjenner du deg igjen i dette, så send inn din søknad med tilhørende CV.

Har du spørsmål, er det bare å ta kontakt med Distribusjonsleder Stig Kokkvold, på mail, stig.kokkvold@posten.no eller tlf. 959 85 810 så kan vi ta en nærmere prat.

Søknad sendes elektronisk, snarest og senest innen søndag 4. oktober 2026.

Ved tilbud om ansettelse må det før tiltredelse fremlegges tilfredsstillende ordinær politiattest, jf. postloven §31 jf. § 25 i forskrift til loven (se www.lovdata.no). Politiattesten skal ikke legges frem før du har mottatt tilbud om ansettelse.

Vi ser frem til å høre fra deg!

title: TMISS Cleared Intelligence Security and Planning Opportunities
description:
Position Overview

Atlas Advisors, LLC is seeking cleared professionals for current and anticipated positions supporting the Theater Military Intelligence Support Services contract and related U.S. military missions throughout Europe.

We are building a qualified candidate bench across a broad range of security, intelligence, collection, planning, screening, and biometric disciplines. These positions will bring together experienced professionals with diverse military, intelligence, security, and technical backgrounds to support critical U.S. missions across the European theater.

Opportunities range from Junior through Journeyman to Senior-level positions. Requirements vary by position and level, and all positions currently require an active Top Secret clearance with SCI eligibility. Your experience could play a critical role in supporting these missions. Review the opportunities below and apply to join the ATLAS team.

Opportunities Available

Cleared American Guards and Construction Surveillance Technicians

Cleared American Guards provide fixed-site protection for secure U.S. facilities. Duties may include access control, personnel and vehicle inspections, monitoring security and alarm systems, maintaining security logs, responding to incidents, enforcing site procedures, and protecting classified facilities and materials.

Construction Surveillance Technicians support the construction or renovation of Sensitive Compartmented Information Facilities and other secure spaces. Duties may include monitoring construction personnel, inspecting tools and materials, reviewing construction plans, identifying unauthorized modifications or security anomalies, controlling access to construction areas, and maintaining detailed construction-security documentation.

These positions require relevant physical-security, force-protection, law-enforcement, construction-security, military, or comparable experience. CST applicants with ICD 705, SCIF construction, construction-trade, engineering, facilities, inspection, or technical surveillance experience are particularly encouraged to apply. Formal ICD 705 training is preferred for CST applicants but is not required to apply.

Security Managers and Special Security Officers

Security Managers and Special Security Officers support personnel, information, physical, and industrial security programs within classified military environments.

Responsibilities may include security-clearance verification, DISS and Scattered Castles administration, access control, badging, Security Clearance Access Rosters, classified-material accountability, security briefings, incident inquiries, inspections, Security Assistance Visits, SCIF administration, secure-area accreditation, document control, NATO security requirements, and security policy implementation.

Applicants should have relevant experience supporting a Command Security Manager, Special Security Officer, personnel security office, G2 security office, SCIF program, or comparable Department of Defense security organization.

Intelligence Analysts All Source OSINT Cyber and CI HUMINT

Intelligence Analysts support military operations and senior-leader decision-making through intelligence research, analysis, production, reporting, and briefings.

Available disciplines include All-Source Intelligence, Open-Source Intelligence, Cyber Intelligence, and Counterintelligence and Human Intelligence.

Responsibilities may include monitoring current events and threat reporting; conducting all-source, open-source, cyber, CI, or HUMINT analysis; producing intelligence assessments and briefings; performing indications and warning analysis; developing threat networks and persons-of-interest profiles; supporting operational planning; responding to intelligence requirements; and using classified and unclassified intelligence databases and analytical tools.

Certain cyber and CI/HUMINT positions may require digital-forensics training, certifications, or directly related technical experience.

Collection Managers

Collection Managers support intelligence collection and requirements management for military intelligence organizations.

Responsibilities may include managing requests for information, coordinating intelligence collection requirements, developing collection plans, supporting intelligence annexes and operational planning, evaluating the use of collection assets, coordinating across intelligence disciplines, maintaining collection-management systems, and conducting quality control of collection and dissemination products.

Applicants should have relevant experience in collection management, intelligence operations, requests for information, intelligence requirements, collection planning, or related military intelligence functions.

Intelligence and Exercise Planners

Intelligence and Exercise Planners support operational planning, contingency planning, crisis-action planning, military exercises, and the integration of intelligence into military decision-making.

Responsibilities may include developing intelligence-planning products, supporting the Military Decision-Making Process, preparing operation orders and task orders, developing exercise scenarios and intelligence injects, participating in Joint Event Life Cycle activities, supporting multinational and NATO exercises, coordinating intelligence architecture and manning, tracking mission-essential tasks, and collaborating with U.S., Joint, Allied, and coalition organizations.

Applicants should have relevant intelligence-planning, operational-planning, exercise-planning, military staff, or joint and multinational planning experience.

Screening Vetting Biometrics and LEP Support

These positions support personnel screening, access determinations, biometric operations, document and media exploitation, watch-list management, and biometric-enabled intelligence.

LEP Screeners may conduct interviews, review records, coordinate with security organizations, maintain screening documentation, support base-access determinations, collect biometric information, and assist with the evaluation of locally employed personnel. Professional Albanian-language capability is required for the current LEP Screener mission.

Biometrics Analysts may support biometric collection systems, document and media exploitation, biometric-enabled intelligence, watch-list management, operational and systems architecture, user training, equipment testing, technical documentation, and coordination with military units and intelligence organizations.

General Qualifications

Requirements vary by role and position level. Candidates must possess:

  • U.S. citizenship.

  • An active Top Secret clearance with SCI eligibility.

  • Relevant education and experience for the applicable Junior, Journeyman, or Senior labor category.

  • The ability to work full-time and on-site at the assigned OCONUS location.

  • The ability to obtain and maintain applicable Status of Forces Agreement, Technical Representative, or other required overseas work authorization.

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills and the ability to support mission-driven priorities in classified or operational environments.

  • The ability to travel, work shifts, or work outside normal duty hours when required by the position.

Education and Experience

This contract includes Junior, Journeyman, and Senior positions. Minimum education and experience requirements vary by role or assignment, and may permit additional directly relevant experience in place of a degree. Candidates should clearly identify their highest degree and years of directly relevant experience.

Overseas Assignment

Positions are located in Germany, Italy, Kosovo, Belgium, and other supported European mission locations. Work is performed full-time and on-site in classified, operational, secure-facility, construction-site, or military environments, depending on the position.

Depending on the position, contract authorization, and individual eligibility, overseas support may include:

  • Relocation assistance

  • Household goods shipment

  • Privately owned vehicle shipment

  • Temporary quarters support

  • Housing allowance

  • Post allowance or cost-of-living allowance

  • Education allowance for eligible dependents

  • Authorized logistical privileges

  • Family-accompanied assignment where permitted

Specific overseas entitlements, travel requirements, work schedules, and family-accompaniment conditions will be confirmed for each opening.

Compensation and Benefits

  • Competitive compensation based on position, location, qualifications, and applicable contract labor rates

  • Comprehensive medical benefits package

  • 401(k) retirement plan with company matching

  • Paid time off

  • Company-provided life insurance

  • Defense Base Act insurance, as applicable

  • Paid training and professional-development opportunities based on position and mission requirements

How to Apply

Submit a current resume identifying the position or discipline that best matches your experience. Include confirmation of an active Top Secret clearance with SCI eligibility, preferred location, highest degree, years of directly relevant experience, relevant military or civilian positions, technical certifications, specialized training, and earliest availability.

Qualified applicants may be contacted regarding current or anticipated positions that match their experience, clearance, qualifications, and location availability.

title: Substation Foreman
description:
Position Summary: The Substation Foreman is responsible for the supervision, assignment and coordination of the Substation Construction and Maintenance activities to ensure a productive workforce that supports all divisional, departmental, site and corporate goals while in accordance with all company policies and local, state, and federal regulations. The Substation Foreman will direct the work and provide technical assistance to subordinates assigned to assist him/her and craft employees working under lump sum and fixed unit price contracts. Oversees job to ensure crew is working safely while performing new construction, maintenance or repair, testing, adjusting and troubleshooting work of substation equipment/systems which includes, but is not limited to, work involving the following:

  • Must supply own safety toed work boots.
  • Must be capable of lifting in excess of 50 lbs.
  • Must be capable of working in confined spaces/areas.
  • Must be able to work independently or with others.
  • Operational experience of various types of heavy equipment :
    • Bucket, derrick and boom trucks
    • Backhoes, excavators and skid steer loaders
    • Articulating Man-lifts
    • Pressure Diggers
    • Trenchers
    • Track Crawler Loader/Backhoe
    • Rough Terrain Telescopic Forklifts
  • Willing to work over-time or long hours during emergency conditions and/or when requested. Schedules can change frequently and with short notice.
  • 90% Travel Required
  • Capable of following Company safety rules and policies.
  • Must have extensive knowledge of construction standard practices, techniques, quality requirements, applicable codes and standards.
  • Must be capable of working in close proximity of energized substation equipment.
  • Must interpret substation structural drawings (i.e. elevations, plan views, section views, grounding details, and foundation plans) and communicate with customers and subordinates.
  • Ability to accurately appraise technical situations and recommend resolutions to problems.
  • Ability to lead/coach subordinates on the crew.
  • Ability to develop and interpret a material list.
  • Ability to trace out phasing in a substation and verify to the three line diagrams.
  • Proficient knowledge in all aspects of substation systems.
  • Ability to determine the proper phase shift and rotation in paralleling transformer banks.
  • Able to direct the daily work of the crew.
  • Have the capability of reading and working from drawings, specifications, procedures, standards, as well as the ability to work within the confines of a project’s performance schedule.
  • Responsibility for all crew members
  • Able to motivate work crew members and develop pride in crew members.
  • Ability to establish grade, elevations, and layout of foundations and cable trough in new and existing stations.
  • Able to work for extended periods in various locations, when requested.
  • Willing to work over-time when requested.
  • Willing to work outside of the normal work schedule including weekends, holidays, and overtime as required for the position.

Physical Demands:

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job.

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to talk or hear. The employee is frequently required to stand; walk; use hands to fingers, handle to feel; and reach with hands and arms.

Work Environment:

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is frequently exposed to fumes or airborne particles, moving mechanical parts and vibration. The employee is occasionally exposed to a variety of extreme conditions at construction job sites. The noise level in the work environment and job sites can be loud. This position is performed in outside weather conditions.

Competencies:

  • Self-Motivated
  • Team-Oriented
  • Customer Oriented
  • Must be able to follow Company safety rules and all other Company policies.

EOE/Minorities/Females/Vet/Disabled

title: DSA DSP
description:
Do you enjoy good company, and doing different and fun activities every day? Our Direct Support Professional position in our Day Support Activities department is the right fit for you. Sunrise Enterprises has worked in Douglas County for over 50 years assisting persons with disabilities to find meaningful employment and achieve self-fulfilling lives.
DETAILS
  • Day Support Activities (Direct Support Professional) - Caregiver
  • Full-Time
  • $17.00/hr.
  • 423 NE Winchester St, Roseburg
QUALIFICATIONS
  • High School Diploma/GED preferred.
  • One year’s experience working with adults with intellectual/developmental disabilities is preferred but not required (training is provided).
  • At least 18 years of age.
  • Strong communication skills, both verbal and written.
  • Positive work ethics, including punctuality, dependability, task completion able to meet deadlines and balance multiple tasks and relationships.
  • Basic computer skills and experience with Microsoft Office products required.
  • Must have proven, stable employment history.
  • Strong organizational skills. Strong verbal, written, open, collaborative, and solutions-oriented communication and teamwork skills.
  • Valid Oregon driver’s license and must be insurable by Sunrise insurance carrier.
  • Proficiency with electronic documentation systems (e.g., SetWorks) preferred.
  • Able to work with limited supervision, displaying initiative and creativity in the workplace.
  • Attention to detail, in order to create documents for reporting purposes.
  • Must be able to pass criminal history checks and drug screen including THC.
  • Ability to obtain CPR and First Aid Certification.
​Working Conditions/Hours
Typically, 7:30 a.m. – 4:00 p.m. Monday – Friday. Overtime, and weekends may be required. Mostly indoors, possible exposure to dust, noise, and various weather conditions.
Physical/Mental Requirements
Must be physically able to assist program participants, including assisted lifting, transfer, and hygiene/personal care if needed. Walking, sitting, stooping, bending, and occasional lifting up to 50 lbs. Driving and transporting trainees and program participants. Ability to multitask and handle/diffuse tense situations. Reasonable accommodations will be made for a person with a disability under ADA.
Essential Functions
  • Assure a high quality of Sunrise Enterprises services are provided to our participants.
  • Participate in transportation duties (transportation for participant activities and/or Meals on Wheels).
  • Assist individuals with disabilities to acquire and develop those skills, behaviors, attitudes, and personal characteristics that will assist them to work, grow, and belong.
  • Provide peri-care for all individuals as needed.
  • Assist supervisor and/or DSA Lead or in providing case management of program participants as directed. This would include goal setting and training that would maximize their potential.
  • Provide support and assistance to supervisor, other DSPs, Services Coordinators, participants, volunteers, and all other staff in the DSA programs.
  • Comply with all applicable federal, state, and local rules and regulations.
  • Do not exceed responsibility/authority that has been delegated by supervisor.
  • Perform job and exhibit good judgment in situations not specifically covered by agency policy and/or procedures.
  • Complete training requirements assigned by department within given deadline.
  • Learn new skills/methods and perform duties as requested by the supervisor in appropriate time frame.
  • Report any incidents of neglect, abuse, emergencies or problems to the supervisor and/or appropriate person per policy.
  • Help develop, implement, and monitor Individual Support Plans (ISPs).
  • Help to maintain and monitor agency records and case files in a professional manner consistent with prescribed guidelines and expectations, e.g. organize, collect data, monitor documentation of participants’ time off requests, case notes, ISPs, time records, and additional information required.
  • Keep relationships with clients professional and limited to work settings and supports. Notify your supervisor of any conflicts of interest due to preexisting relationships with trainees.
  • Submit time sheets and other required documentation in a timely and accurate manner.
  • Attend and participate in required meetings, trainings, and committees.
  • Maintain a safe work environment.
  • Serve as a role model for participants and other staff.
  • Observe scheduled work hours and days. Facilitate and participate in team meetings, staff meetings, and ISP meetings when necessary.
  • Perform duties and complete tasks as requested by supervisor in a reasonable amount of time.
  • Attend and participate in required meetings, trainings, and committees.
  • Do not exceed responsibility/authority delegated to you by supervisor.
  • Exhibit good judgment in situations not specifically covered by agency policy or procedures.
  • Keep work area in a clean, safe condition.
  • Submit timesheets and other required documentation in a timely and accurate manner.
  • Meet regular attendance requirements at assigned worksite because job requires face-to-face interaction with participants, customers, or other employees.
  • Report any incidents of negligence, abuse, emergencies, or problems to the appropriate agency, person, or supervisor per company policies and procedures.
  • Keep relationships with participants professional and limited to work settings and supports. Notify your supervisor of any conflicts of interest due to preexisting relationships with participants.
  • Other duties as assigned.
If you are ready to use your skills, personality, and ambitions to better our community and the lives of the people here, join our team by applying for the Direct Support Professional position today.

title: Store Director
description:
Albertsons' Northern California Market has an opening for a Store Director.

The Store Director is responsible for the day-to-day operations of the store. The Store Director has overall responsibility for the store operation and employees. The Store Director is responsible for making store-level decisions on hiring, training, disciplinary action, and scheduling. The Company expects the Store Director will spend more than half their time in directing others, managing the enterprise, and activities directly and closely related to those tasks and that anyone having difficulty doing will inform their District Manager and/or Human Resources so that additional training can be provided.

Responsibilities

  • Overall management responsibility for the operation of a retail grocery store. This includes but not limited to store performance, control of cash, inventory and security, customer service, and management of staff
  • Track, analyze and take action to improve store performance by forecasting of weekly/daily sales goals and meeting or exceeding established goals.
  • Communicate sales goals, department performance and sales opportunities with staff to ensure positive results
  • Forecast, schedule, and monitor labor to be consistent with store sales and productivity guidelines and wage budgets; create action plan to address cost control issues
  • Develop and direct the execution of strategies to improve product placement and appearance
  • Manage display accuracy and appearance to implement promotions. Ensure that products are properly displayed and ordered in a manner to maintain in-stock conditions.
  • Manage issues relating to store maintenance, cleanliness, safety and sanitation.
  • Oversee and manage handling of cash and accounting. Ensure store is secured.
  • Prioritize, plan, and coordinate work activities, and manage time and resources so that work objectives are timely met.
  • Ensure compliance with legal requirements and company policies and procedures, including money handling, check cashing, security, food safety, worker and customer safety, sanitation, consumer protection laws (e.g., recalls), accurate and timely payment of wages, etc.
  • Focus on customer satisfaction and needs, ensure that employees provide customers with superior customer service through use of best practices and training and coaching concerning the importance of superior customer service
  • Handle customer and employee complaints. Makes decisions to resolve all complaints in the best possible manner for the customer or employee and the business.
  • Select, train, develop, and manage job performance of store employees, with input from other management personnel; expected to effectively recommend hiring and disciplinary action up to and including termination.
  • Provide constructive suggestions and encouragement, set performance expectations, provide honest feedback, and identify assignments to provide others with developmental opportunities.
  • Maintain appropriate professional relationship with union officials, and ensure compliance with collective bargaining agreement provisions, if applicable.
  • Maintain positive working relationships with direct reports, peers, supervisors, suppliers, and customers effectively handling complex or difficult situations involving others.
  • Motivate others to perform the job and work towards common objectives. Comply with Company policies and procedures to serve as a role model to others instilling a positive attitude in others.
  • Responsible for ensuring the store is properly staffed to meet labor goals, sales goals, and customer needs. Takes a proactive approach to hiring and in engaged in what staff is needed to run an efficient operation.
  • Makes the final decision on hiring candidates, conducts interviews, and meets with prospective employees.
  • Ensures new hires are aware of all policies, procedures, and receive the proper/required training. Evaluates new hires, provides feedback, and makes final decision on a new hire’s eligibility to pass the probationary period.

Internal applicants must pass Store Director Selection (SDS) interview process prior to placement in the role.

Qualifications

  • Education Level: High School Diploma (or equivalent) required; College degree preferred
  • Experience Level
  • Three years Store Manager experience responsible for managing a department/team within a multi-department operation within retail, hospitality, or service industry required or five or more years retail or managerial experience in an Assistant Manager capacity required
  • Retail grocery experience required
  • Skills and Experiences
  • Strong planning and organizational skills; strong math and analytical skills.
  • Demonstrated prior customer service and supervisory skills or related experience.
  • Strong understanding of overall retail store operations.
  • Strong leadership and communication skills, both verbal and written.
  • Computer literate.
  • Ability to make quality decisions while working under time constraints.
  • Ability to get along with others.
  • Travel Requirements: None
  • Physical Environment
  • Ability to sit, stand or walk for extended periods of time.
  • Ability to reach, lift, stack, and maneuver objects of varying dimensions and weights up to approximately 55 lbs.
  • May spend long periods of time at desk or computer terminal.
  • May use calculators, keyboards, telephone, computers and other office equipment in the course of normal workday.
  • Stooping, bending, twisting, and reaching may be required in completion of some job duties.
  • Workday is fast paced; Holiday, evening and weekend work may be required.

Albertsons Companies' Northern California Market office is located in Pleasanton, CA and supports the operations of 285 retail stores across northern California, northwestern Nevada, and Hawaii under the Safeway, Andronico’s, Vons, and Pak ‘n Save Foods banners.


Why you will choose us
Albertsons Companies has always been a people-oriented business, and thoughtful people practices remain a core element of our company’s philosophy. As friendly, enthusiastic people who enjoy offering customers an exceptional shopping experience, we provide world-class customer service each and every day.

We also provide a variety of benefits including:

Candidates with unique qualifications may be considered for compensation above this range. title: Test & Instrumentation Development Engineer
description:
At Apple, individual creativity converges around shared values that drive innovation. Our products emerge from collaborative teams strengthening each other's ideas, fueled by diverse perspectives and a belief we can transform lives. Ready to make an impact?

The Instrumentation and Test technology team architects and designs best-in-class, end-to-end test and measurements systems.

We are a collaborative group of creative and thoughtful people developing highly complex and sophisticated systems to validate the performance of sensors and other critical technologies in our world-class products.

This individual will play a key role in designing comprehensive test strategies, methodologies, and integrating the measurement systems to support new product introduction, characterization, ramp, and mass production. This includes everything from defining high level test plans to architecting the specific instruments required to execute them.

Minimum Qualifications

  • We are looking for a systems-thinking engineer ready to take ownership of complex test solutions. Our ideal candidate has experience in test integration, implementation, and has a strong foundation in at least one of the following core areas: system or application-level test software or instrumentation hardware design.
  • Master’s degree in Electrical Engineering or Computer Science
  • 3+ years of experience in a programming language like C/C++ or Python
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with an ability to collaborate with cross-functional engineering and design teams.
  • Hands-on experience applying generative AI or LLM-based tools to engineering work – code generation, data analysis, documentation, or failure triage.
  • Excellent skills in debugging and performing failure analysis across software, hardware and system domains.
  • Experience with structured problem-solving methodologies like Design of Experiments (DOE).
  • Ability to perform and interpret statistical data analysis

Preferred Qualifications

  • End-to-end Test Design: Experience creating and documenting comprehensive test plans, defining test cases and coverage, and developing validation methodologies for complex systems.
  • Curiosity and Adaptability: You are driven by curiosity, energized by solving novel problems, and motivated to learn new skills to get the job done.
  • Focused Problem Solving: You excel at identifying the most critical variables in a complex system and can develop a clear, focused plan of action even when all the details are not yet available.
  • Hands-on experience with electronics debugging tools
  • Electrical engineering fundamentals (ability to read schematics & layout & component datasheets).
  • You have experience developing robust software and algorithms in a modern object-oriented or scripting language (e.g., Python, C++). Familiarity with the Apple ecosystem is a plus but not required.
  • Background in testing high-volume consumer electronics, particularly with Touch, Sensing, Display, or other complex user-facing technologies.
  • Knowledge of digital signal processing (DSP) or image processing algorithms.
  • Experience with instrument camera and optical capture system is a plus.
  • Interest in building AI workflow: experience developing scripts, agents, or tooling that wraps a LLM around existing processes to reduce manual overhead.

title: Supervisor, Inside Retention - Tupelo, MS
description:

The candidate can expect to work in the office full time (100%). The office location for this position is: 499 South Gloster, Ste B2 – Tupelo, MS 38801 and all candidates should be able to commute to this location.

I. Job Summary

Supervises the Retention Desk. The Retention Desk consists of 11 Account Associates that take inbound cancellation request call activity. Manage the Area's account retention program and assign retention responsibility to the appropriate Account Associate.


II. Essential Duties and Responsibilities

  • Work with leadership to establish and or refine cancellation processes. These processes would include: Call Flow, MAS Cancellation Ticket Process, Communication protocol between Cancel Desk and Market Area’s. Tracking and reporting procedures, etc...
  • Establish and or refine Coaching and Training Protocol using RESPOND training as basis. This would include: Daily, Weekly, and Monthly training regiments for individual representatives as well as the team. Coaching should consist of desk side activity as well as remote listening and performance measurement.
  • Assist in the implementation and ongoing development of the Cancellation Desk.
  • Generates revenue by retaining existing customers and executing the Area’s Sales & Marketing Plan to achieve revenue goals by sales channel ensuring internal revenue growth through additional services, and maintaining profitability on retained accounts.
  • Maintains and reinforces the corporate sales strategy and design with the Retention Team.
  • Handle any escalated customer calls. These calls may include when a customer requests to speak with a Supervisor or with any other customer call.
  • Establishes and maintains a high level of customer satisfaction on all transactions with existing customers. Communicates to and works with the Inside Sales Manager to help resolve unique customer issues/concerns.
  • Supervises activities of the Account Associate retention department. Ensures team members meet or exceed goals for cancellations, proactive retention, pricing, service upgrades, referral generation and productivity, along with other possible metrics as defined by the position of an Account Associate.
  • Forecasts and recruits qualified candidates for available and/or upgraded retention positions.
  • Maintains an ongoing training, coaching and mentoring program to upgrade the skills of assigned retention personnel and develop their opportunities for promotion, if available.
  • Establishes and maintains an ongoing proactive account retention program, which includes meeting customer retention goals.
  • Works with the Inside Sales Manager to communicate and effectively manage the Area’s price increase strategies including meeting price increase goals.
  • Effectively maintains and ensures the use of WM sales tools (i.e. Record Setter, Proposal Master, MAS, Pricing Tools, etc.). Ensures that the entire Account Associate Team is well trained in the use of these tools.
  • Analyze lost business trends and recommends corrective actions.
  • Provides industry knowledge and interpretation of regulations to customers.
  • Participates in and takes ownership of municipal account retention when and if required.
  • Regularly meets with customer executives to ensure client needs are met and expectations exceeded.


III. Qualifications

A. Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's Degree Sales/Marketing, Business Administration or similar area of study
  • 5 years in Sales/Marketing, Business Administration or similar area


B. Preferred Qualifications

  • Internal applicants should have demonstrated leadership qualities on their current team in order to be considered.

Listed below are key points regarding physical demands, physical and occupational risks, and the work environment of the job. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of the job. Office: This job primarily operates in a professional office environment and routinely requires the use of standard office equipment such as computers, phones, copy machines, etc.

At WM, each eligible employee receives a competitive total compensation package including Medical, Dental, Vision, Life Insurance and Short Term Disability. As well as a Stock Purchase Plan, Company match on 401K, and more! Our employees also receive Paid Vacation, Holidays, and Personal Days. Please note that benefits may vary by site.

title: Pharmacy Tech I
description:
Job Summary

The Pharmacy Technician supports the delivery of safe and effective pharmaceutical care by assisting in medication preparation, distribution, and inventory management. This role ensures the smooth operation of the pharmacy by maintaining compliance with regulatory standards, providing excellent customer service, and supporting healthcare professionals in delivering optimal patient care.

Essential Functions
  • Assists in the preparation and dispensing of medications, including compounding, labeling, and verifying medication orders under the supervision of a licensed pharmacist.
  • Maintains accurate inventory levels by monitoring stock, ordering supplies, and conducting regular inventory audits to ensure the availability of medications and pharmacy supplies.
  • Provides excellent customer service by answering questions from patients and healthcare staff regarding medications and pharmacy services, ensuring a positive experience.
  • Maintains accurate records of medication orders, dispensing activities, and inventory transactions in compliance with hospital policies and regulatory requirements.
  • Participates in quality assurance activities, including medication storage checks and compliance with safety standards, to promote safe medication practices.
  • Ensures that pharmacy equipment is functioning properly and assist in troubleshooting any issues that arise.
  • Works closely with pharmacists and other healthcare professionals to facilitate effective communication and coordinate patient care.
  • Stays current with pharmacy practices and participate in ongoing training and educational opportunities.
  • Performs other duties as assigned.
  • Maintains regular and reliable attendance.
  • Complies with all policies and standards.
Qualifications
  • 0-2 years of experience in a hospital Pharmacy required
Knowledge, Skills and Abilities
  • Knowledge of pharmaceutical practices including medication preparation, dispensing, and compounding under supervision.
  • Understanding of regulatory compliance and safety standards, including HIPAA, OSHA, and state/federal pharmacy laws.
  • Proficiency in inventory management techniques to maintain accurate stock levels and timely ordering of medications and supplies.
  • Ability to operate pharmacy equipment and troubleshoot minor technical issues effectively.
  • Strong communication skills to provide excellent customer service and collaborate with healthcare professionals.
  • Detail-oriented and organized to ensure accuracy in medication labeling, documentation, and compliance activities.
  • Ability to adapt to a fast-paced environment and prioritize tasks effectively to support patient care needs.
  • Proficiency with pharmacy-related software and basic computer skills for managing records, orders, and patient information.
Licenses and Certifications
  • PHAR-C - Certified Pharmacy Tech preferred

title: C Lineman - Transmission
description:
Position Summary:

The Class C Lineman Transmission is an entry level lineman position in the construction, maintenance and repair of electrical transmission systems. This position works at various locations. The position may also be required to travel to another state depending on customer demands.

Essential Functions:

  • Work safely while performing new construction, maintenance or repair work of energized and de-energized transmission work.
  • Stringing overhead wire.
  • Setting poles and anchors.
  • Frequently works with energized high voltage systems requiring skill and care to protect the lives of themselves and others.
  • Maintains company vehicles, equipment and tools in good working order.
  • Does all other related work as required to complete the job.
  • Must be able to work outside, frequently in inclement weather.
  • Able to perform rigorous physical labor.
  • Capable of learning transmission voltages on a circuit.
  • Must be familiar with induced voltage.
  • Capable of safely setting a pole.
  • Capable of learning to understand and read blueprints.
  • Capable of assisting with inspecting and recognizing structural problems.
  • Able to work productively from an aerial device.
  • Capable of assisting in troubleshooting.
  • Able to work alone on de-energized lines.
  • Capable of obtaining knowledge of wire stringing techniques.
  • Capable of learning and understanding how to sag wire from structure or bucket.
  • Able to assist with assembly and erect towers to all heights.
  • Able to assist with working from an aerial ladder to catch off and clip in.
  • Able to assist in framing and setting most basic line structures.
  • Able to assist in framing a de-energized pole structure in the air.
  • Able to assist with installing all types of compression connections.
  • Capable of working at heights and/or confined spaces.
  • Capable of properly installing and removing PPE and cover up.
  • Capable of properly inspecting rubber goods, covers and PPE.
  • Must be able to climb different types of structures (wood, steel, etc.) and possess the necessary tools to do so.
  • Understands how to tie various lineman knots.
  • Capable of making up and using a hand line.
  • Understands grounding procedures.
  • Understands proper equipment set-up and grounding procedures.
  • Understands how and when to use Kellum grips.
  • Able to identify different types of materials used in line work.
  • Understands minimum approach distance.
  • Understands flag and tag procedures.
  • Capable of performing basic bucket rescue/escape.

Minimum Requirements:

  • 1-year minimum of field experience.
  • Able to read and communicate effectively in English.
  • Able to obtain a Commercial Driver’s License permit within 60 days of employment.
  • A Commercial Driver’s License is preferred.
  • Able to travel long distances on short notice, when required.
  • Able to work for extended periods in various locations, when required.
  • Able to lift in excess of 50 lbs.
  • Able to properly inspect rubber goods and PPE.
  • Willing to work over-time when requested.
  • Willingness to glove/work live high voltage transmission lines.
  • Willing to work outside of the normal work schedule including weekends, holidays, and overtime as required for the position.


Physical Demands:
The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job.

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to talk or hear. The employee is frequently required to stand; walk; use hands to finger, handle, and feel; and reach with hands and arms.

title: Football Student Filmer (WS-ST1)
description:
Job Title: Football Student Filmer (WS-ST1)

Classification: Student Employee (non-exempt)

Name and Address of Employer: St. Olaf College, 1520 St. Olaf Ave, Northfield, MN 55057

If the position requires the student to work off campus, provide the name and address here:


Department Name: Football

Unit Number (5 digits): 11707

Length of Position: See Employment Authorization

Contact Person/Supervisor: Head Football Coach

Wage Range: $12.00-13.00/hour


Description of the Position: (Purpose of the Position):

The Football Filmer plays a vital role in the success of the St. Olaf Football program. This position is responsible for capturing high-quality video of all practices and games using multiple filming systems, including elevated camera platforms, press-box setups, remote filming stations (such as Skifter Hall), end-zone EVS telescoping systems, and drone technology.

You will receive full training on how to operate every piece of equipment and how to film from each location. High-quality video is essential to our program—without it we cannot effectively teach, evaluate, or develop our players.

This position requires a detail-oriented individual who is coachable, takes instruction well, and takes pride in consistently producing high-quality work. The Football Filmer must understand how to capture proper angles, maintain steady shots, zoom appropriately, and follow specific filming standards so our coaching staff can fully utilize the footage.



Transferable Skills:

Working as a Football Filmer helps develop several valuable skills that can be applied in many academic, professional, and real-world settings:

Attention to Detail

  • Learning how to track plays, frame shots, adjust angles, and follow strict filming guidelines develops precision and discipline.

Coachability and Taking Instruction

  • Filmers learn to receive feedback, make corrections quickly, and follow exact steps—skills that translate directly into any team-oriented workplace.

Technical Proficiency

  • Operating drones, cameras, tripods, EVS telescoping systems, and remote filming setups builds confidence with technology and equipment.

Situational Awareness

  • Anticipating plays, staying focused for long periods, and adjusting equipment in real time develop awareness and the ability to stay calm under pressure.

Time Management and Reliability

  • Practices and games adhere to strict timelines; filmers must show up early, prepare equipment, and deliver consistent performance.

Responsibility and Care for High-Value Equipment

  • Managing thousands of dollars’ worth of equipment teaches responsibility, organization, and professionalism.



Duties and Responsibilities:

Primary Filming Responsibilities

  • Film all football practices from designated locations, including drone operation when assigned.

  • Film all games from press-box platforms, Skifter Hall remote locations, or the EVS end-zone telescoping system.

  • Follow the program’s filming standards for angle, framing, zooming, and timing.

  • Ensure all plays and periods are accurately captured without gaps or missed reps.

  • Communicate with coaches regarding shot quality and any issues during filming.

Equipment Care & Management

  • Treat all equipment (cameras, tripods, EVS systems, drones, batteries, memory cards, etc.) with exceptional care.

  • Complete pre-practice and pre-game equipment checks to ensure everything is charged, functional, and ready to use.

  • Safely store and transport all equipment before and after practices and games.

  • Report any damage, malfunction, or missing equipment immediately to the coaching staff.

Technical & Support Tasks

  • Learn and apply proper drone operation, including launching, tracking, and landing safely.

  • Assist in setting up filming locations (press box, end-zone tower, Skifter Hall remotes) before practices and games.

  • Upload, label, and properly organize film after practices and games when instructed.

  • Maintain familiarity with equipment manuals and safety procedures.

  • Support coaching staff with additional video needs (special projects, cut-ups, player highlights) when requested.

Professional Expectations

  • Arrive on time and be prepared for all practice and game assignments.

  • Be focused and attentive for the entire duration of filming.

  • Dress appropriately for outdoor filming in all weather conditions.

  • Protect player and team confidentiality at all times—no sharing of film or footage.


Qualifications: (Education/Experience/Skills) No prior experience required.

Physical and Environmental Factors:

This position requires operating equipment to perform the essential functions. It may also require exposure to extreme cold or extreme heat to perform the essential functions. Candidates must possess the ability to safely perform the physical work required of all duties with or without reasonable accommodation.

This job description is for general information purposes. It is not intended to list all duties and responsibilities of the position. This job description is subject to change at any time by St. Olaf College, with or without prior notice.

title: Director of Data Analysis - Office Information Technology
description:
ABOUT OUR DISTRICT:

The Syracuse City School District is undergoing a new phase of innovation and transformation with the goal of ensuring that all students graduate high school with the skills needed to be ready for college and career. For Syracuse, all means all. The School Board and Syracuse community have charged the Superintendent with improving student achievement, and she is seeking a dedicated and diverse team of educators to partner with her in moving the district toward its goals.

The Syracuse City School District represents 35 schools and programs, including 6 high schools, 6 middle schools, 6 K-8 schools, 13 elementary schools, and 4 alternative education programs, serving approximately 19,000 students Pre-K–12. Of these students, 82.3% qualify for free or reduced-price lunch, 20.1% are served by the Office of Special Education, and 83% are students of color.

Location: Office of Information Technology

DISTINGUISHING FEATURES OF THIS CLASS:

The work involves responsibility for directing and managing the Syracuse City School District's data analysis, reporting, and evaluation functions. The incumbent provides leadership and supervision to professional and technical staff engaged in the collection, analysis, interpretation, and dissemination of student, instructional, operational, and accountability data. The position is responsible for establishing districtwide data governance practices, prioritizing analytical projects, coordinating responses to data requests, and ensuring the availability of accurate and timely information to support strategic planning, school improvement, and operational decision-making. The incumbent works closely with district leadership to develop data systems, performance measures, and reporting processes that advance District goals. General supervision is exercised over professional, technical, and support staff. Work is performed under the general direction of the Assistant Superintendent of Information Technology and Accountability or other higher-level administrator with latitude for independent judgment. Does related work as required.

TYPICAL WORK ACTIVITIES:

  • Directs, supervises, and evaluates the work of professional and technical staff assigned to the District Data Team.
  • Establishes departmental goals, priorities, performance expectations, and workflow processes for districtwide data operations.
  • Develops and implements procedures governing the collection, validation, analysis, security, and dissemination of student, staff, financial, operational, and accountability data using District platform.
  • Oversees the management of data-related requests through established service platforms, ensuring timely and accurate responses to schools and departments.
  • Establishes systems for prioritizing analytical projects and balancing competing district needs and deadlines.
  • Partners with senior district leadership and building principals to identify data, reports, analyses, and performance measures necessary to support strategic initiatives and organizational decision-making.
  • Directs the preparation and presentation of district, school, and program evaluation reports.
  • Oversees the development of dashboards, data visualization tools, scorecards, and reporting systems used by district and school leaders.
  • Leads the development and implementation of data governance standards, procedures, and quality-control practices.
  • Collaborates with building principals and district administrators to ensure access to accurate, timely, and actionable information supporting instructional and operational improvement efforts.
  • Provides leadership in analyzing student achievement, attendance, enrollment, graduation, accountability, assessment, staffing, and operational data.
  • Oversees the preparation and submission of required federal, state, regional, and local reports.
  • Coordinates data management activities with the Regional Information Center, New York State Education Department, and other external agencies.
  • Directs program evaluation activities, including data collection, survey administration, statistical analyses, and outcome measurement.
  • Develops policies and procedures related to data reporting, records management, and data integrity.
  • Provides training and technical assistance to administrators and staff regarding data systems, data interpretation, and data-informed decision making.
  • May serve as an advisor to district leadership on emerging trends, best practices, and innovations in educational data analysis and accountability.


FULL PERFORMANCE KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, ABILITIES AND PERSONAL CHARACTERISTICS

  • Good knowledge of school district staff needs and responsibilities.
  • Thorough knowledge of the principles, practices and methods of statistical analyses and evaluation design.
  • Good knowledge of educational theories, trends, and accountability systems.
  • Ability to supervise, oversee, and evaluate the work of professional and technical staff.
  • Ability to establish priorities, manage workflow, and meet specific goals set by district administration.
  • Ability to maintain effective working relationships with groups and individuals.
  • Ability to train staff and provide technical assistance.
  • Ability to read and comprehend complex oral and written material.
  • Ability to clearly and concisely express ideas orally and in writing, including technology-based communications.
  • Ability to develop and implement procedures related to data collection, analysis, and reporting.
  • Tact; resourcefulness; initiative; and leadership ability.


MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:

Promotion: Two (2) years of permanent competitive class status as a Senior Data Analyst (Educational Research and Evaluation). OR;

Open Competitive:

A. Graduation from a regionally accredited or New York State registered college or university with a Master’s Degree in Instructional Design, Instructional Technology, Educational Psychology, Statistics, Public Administration, Business Administration, Economics, Research, Education, Sociology, Political Science or Psychology or a closely related field and one (1) year of supervisory or lead professional experience involving educational research, evaluation, institutional planning, data collection, and data analysis; OR

B. Graduation from a regionally accredited or New York State registered college or university with a Bachelor's Degree as defined in (A) above and two (2) years of experience, or its part-time equivalent, as described in (A), including supervisory or lead responsibilities; OR

C. Six (6) years of experience, or its part-time equivalent, in educational research, evaluation, institutional planning, data collection, and data analysis, including supervisory or lead responsibilities.

SALARY

Salary and benefits pursuant to the Unit 11 Collective Bargaining Agreement with a starting salary range of $116,965-$150,383 depending on qualifications and experience.
