title: Safety and Security Supervisor (Nashville)
description:
About the Work Unit:

Vanderbilt University Public Safety (VUPS) is led by the Office of the Chief of Police in the Division of Administration. VUPS is a dedicated team of over 400 professionals united by a shared commitment to fostering a safe, secure, and welcoming environment for all in the Vanderbilt community. Organized into several specialized units, our department includes commissioned officers, security professionals, and skilled administrative staff, all working collaboratively to uphold the highest standards of community-based policing.

Key Functions and Expected Performance:

Leadership & Administration

  • Lead an assigned unit/shift, directly supervising safety and security staff, which will include: Weapons Detection Specialists, Community Service Officers (CSOs), and Safety and Security Specialists, and ensuring adequate resource allocation.
  • Train, re-train, and educate staff on weapons detection systems and security protocols. Conduct quarterly performance evaluations, provide coaching, and manage performance conversations and necessary counseling.
  • Maintain and update the shift schedule, review/approve timesheets, and time off/leave requests. Serve as operational backup for Weapons Detection Specialists and CSOs as needed.
  • Conduct routine audits of operational processes, personnel inspections, and equipment checks to ensure adherence to departmental and regulatory compliance.
  • Prepare and review all appropriate reports and documents submitted by direct reports. Keep management informed of significant security events, prepare activity reports, and participate in management and key stakeholder meetings.
  • Lead accountability measures to ensure fair and impartial service delivery. Conduct preliminary investigations into employee misconduct complaints, providing disciplinary recommendations to management when warranted.

Security Operations & Calls for Service

  • Conduct individual building security checks and directed patrols. Respond to general calls for service, including building access/lock-ups, motorist assists (vehicle access, jump starts), and personal safety escorts.
  • Assist with emergency response (fire/medical), including secure transportation and aiding medical personnel in the detention of psychiatric patients.
  • Conduct bi-weekly Emergency Phone Tests for the assigned zone.
  • Provide backup for other officers/personnel as necessary.

Community Engagement & Special Events

  • Proactively patrol assigned areas to identify potential security risks. Lead problem-solving initiatives through community partnerships to develop crime prevention strategies.
  • Coordinate with Community Relations personnel regarding physical security, safety information, and crime prevention issues within the area of responsibility.
  • Provide required security, crowd control, and order maintenance for special events, including athletic events, concerts, commencement, and visiting dignitaries.

Performs other duties as assigned.

Supervisory Relationships:

The Safety and Security Supervisor is responsible for the assigned Safety and Security personnel during shift operations. This position reports administratively and functionally to the Safety and Security Manager(s) as assigned, and the Safety and Security Director.

Education and Certifications

  • Must possess a High School Diploma or G.E.D. and have a minimum of three (3) years of proven experience as a security officer or equivalent role, with at least one (1) year of supervisory experience.

  • Must successfully complete the department field training program and all required VUPS training (De-escalation, Pressure Point Control Tactics, CPR/AED certification, and CSO training), and demonstrate knowledge of all University and Police Department written directives, rules, and regulations within 30 days of hire.
  • Must possess and maintain a valid Driver's License and a satisfactory driving record (subject to continuous third-party monitoring).

Experience and Skills:

  • Proven ability to supervise and guide staff, develop personnel skills, provide constructive feedback, and handle disciplinary issues. Must exhibit the willingness and ability to make timely, sound, fact-based decisions and accept responsibility.

  • Must remain calm and objective during stressful or unpleasant situations, demonstrating self-restraint in challenging circumstances.

  • Excellent demonstrated written and oral communication and public speaking skills. Must be able to establish and maintain effective working relationships with the public, enforcement officials, and diverse university/medical center constituencies (students, faculty, staff, parents).

  • Excellent customer service skills and demonstrated problem-solving skills are essential. Must be able to organize, prioritize, and manage multiple tasks independently.

  • Experience working with Microsoft Word, Excel, and other computer programs is preferred.

Working Conditions and Physical Requirements

  • Must be able to stand for long periods, walk, climb, and lift. Must meet written departmental standards for appearance and grooming.
  • Must pass a thorough background investigation and drug test demonstrating good moral character, a good driving record, and no prior criminal convictions that would prohibit certification under the State of Tennessee Private Protective Services Act.
  • Must be available to work nights, weekends, and holidays and be willing to work in inclement weather and various weather extremes.
  • Must be able to use necessary precautionary equipment (e.g., TB mask) and may encounter hazardous materials, infectious disease, blood-borne pathogens, loud noises, and potential physical danger from violent individuals.
  • Must obtain required immunizations and medical tests to work in patient care and high-risk areas.

title: Senior Systems Testing / QA Specialist
description:
Assignment: IT26 32564C – Sr Tester/QA INS Tools – Voluntary Mergers of PHUs
Client: Ontario Public Sector – Health Services Cluster
Location: Toronto, ON – 5700 Yonge Street
Work Arrangement: 100% Onsite
Start Date: October 1, 2026
End Date: October 5, 2027
Schedule: Monday–Friday, 7.25 hours/day between 8:00 AM–5:00 PM, excluding lunch
Security Clearance: CRJMC
Openings: 1
Submission Limit: Maximum 1 candidate
Closing Date: September 21, 2026 at 12:00 PM
Position Overview
Our client is seeking a Senior Systems Testing/QA Specialist to provide technical leadership and hands-on testing expertise for complex public-sector healthcare applications and tools.
The successful candidate will be responsible for planning, coordinating and executing comprehensive functional and non-functional system testing across iPHIS, OHISS, TIS and Inspections Tools. The role will support application enhancements, integrations, defect resolutions, routine and incident management, production releases and other mission-critical healthcare initiatives.
The Senior QA Specialist will work closely with developers, architects, product owners, business stakeholders and other project team members to develop effective test strategies and ensure applications meet quality, business and client acceptance requirements.
Key Responsibilities
  • Perform functional and non-functional system testing of iPHIS, OHISS, TIS and Inspections Tools, including program requirements, application integrations, enhancements and defect resolutions.
  • Provide ongoing testing support for routine and incident management activities involving public health units and program areas.
  • Develop complete testing documentation and artifacts, including test strategies, test plans, test cases/use cases, test scripts, automated test scripts, test results reports and defect logs.
  • Translate functional, business and system knowledge into effective test planning and execution.
  • Create test data according to established test plans.
  • Analyze test results, perform retesting and confirm expected outcomes.
  • Participate in walkthroughs and reviews with users and ensure client acceptance criteria are met.
  • Recommend changes where testing results do not meet required standards.
  • Retest implementation criteria in live/production environments and recommend user sign-off.
  • Work closely with developers, architects, product owners and other stakeholders to establish effective test plans based on feature and requirements documentation.
  • Provide QA and technical expertise to identify, track and resolve testing, production and IT-related issues.
  • Provide technical leadership, guidance and oversight to junior testers and coordinate testing activities across multiple work streams.


Requirements

Mandatory Qualifications & Experience
1. Public Sector & Healthcare Experience – Mandatory
Candidates must have:
  • 5+ years of experience working with federal, provincial or broader public-sector healthcare providers.
  • Knowledge of Public Sector Enterprise Architecture artifacts, processes and practices, with the ability to produce technical documentation aligned with industry standards.
  • In-depth knowledge of Project Management Institute (PMI) and public-sector I&IT project management methodologies.
  • Knowledge and experience working on public-sector health-related projects.
  • Knowledge and understanding of Ministry policies and IT project approval processes and requirements.
  • Experience adopting and adhering to:
    • Public Sector Unified I&IT Project Methodology
    • Public Sector Enterprise Architecture
    • Public Sector Gating Process
    • OPS Standard Systems Development Methodologies
  • Experience working on large, complex IT healthcare projects.
2. Senior QA & Systems Testing Experience – Mandatory
Candidates must have 7+ years of experience in the following:
  • Acting as a Lead Systems Testing/QA Specialist, providing guidance and oversight to junior testers.
  • Planning, organizing and implementing testing efforts, including preparation of test plans and coordination of test execution.
  • Knowledge and understanding of testing methods within an object-oriented environment.
  • All stages of system testing, including:
    • Test strategy
    • Testing tool selection
    • Test planning
    • Test case preparation
    • Test data preparation
    • Manual test execution
    • Automated test execution
    • Defect logging and tracking
  • Testing:
    • Clinical systems
    • Mission-critical systems
    • High-volume transactional systems
    • Highly available environments
  • Knowledge and experience with structured methodologies for the development, design, implementation and maintenance of applications.
3. Application, Integration & Web Services Testing – Mandatory
Hands-on experience performing functional and non-functional testing of:
  • Commercial Off-the-Shelf (COTS) solutions, including:
    • Patches
    • New releases
    • Acceptance testing
    • Enhancement requests
    • Regression testing
  • In-house web applications.
  • HL7-FHIR-based web services.
  • RESTful / JSON / XML interfaces.
  • Application Programming Interfaces (APIs).
  • Reporting solutions.
  • Integration components.
  • Extensions and enhancements.
  • Product modules and cross-system integrations.
  • Ontario Health-related systems such as Client Registry, Provider Registry and Audit Services, or equivalent complex healthcare systems.
4. Security & Authentication Testing – Mandatory
Experience testing security components using:
  • SAML
  • JWT
Candidates must also be capable of producing and interpreting security and performance testing results for defect reviews with clients, partners and project teams.
5. Test Automation & Testing Tools – Mandatory
Experience with:
  • Developing automated test scripts using tools/frameworks such as Selenium.
  • Executing automated test scripts.
  • API testing tools for querying and testing interfaces at the messaging layer.
  • Web service testing using tools such as:
    • Rational ClearQuest
    • SOAP UI
    • Postman
    • Programming languages
  • Test management and defect tracking tools such as:
    • Jira
    • Confluence
    • TestRail.
6. SQL, Data & Information Retrieval – MUST HAVE
This is specifically identified as a MUST HAVE by the client.
Candidates must have:
  • Knowledge and experience with information retrieval packages.
  • Experience performing data queries and ad-hoc queries using SQL.
  • Knowledge of other query languages.
  • Ability to analyze and validate data to support system and application testing.
Candidates without strong SQL/data-query experience should not be submitted.
7. Accessibility Testing – Mandatory
Experience performing accessibility testing of:
  • Websites
  • Web content
  • Mobile applications
Candidates must understand WCAG 2.0 and have experience using tools that support web accessibility testing in accordance with AODA legislation.
8. Business Intelligence Testing – Mandatory
Experience testing Business Intelligence (BI) solutions, including:
  • Test planning and preparation.
  • Data setup and integration.
  • Validating BI data.
  • Testing predefined analytical reports.
  • Testing ad-hoc reporting tools.
  • Testing dashboards.
  • Validating:
    • Accuracy
    • Completeness
    • Data integrity
Candidates must also be able to review business and technical requirements from a testing perspective, including requirements related to BI solutions.
9. SDLC, Agile & DevOps – Mandatory
Candidates must have:
  • Knowledge and experience working within traditional and Agile teams.
  • Experience with standard DevOps processes and tools.
  • Knowledge and experience with at least one programming language.
  • Knowledge and experience across all phases of the Systems Development Life Cycle (SDLC).
  • Ability to review business and technical documentation from a testing perspective and identify issues early in the SDLC.
  • Knowledge and understanding of Information Management principles, concepts, policies and practices.
Defect Management & QA Governance
The successful candidate must have 7+ years of experience with:
  • Identifying and documenting issues and risks.
  • Creating and maintaining defect logs and defect summary reports.
  • Using defect/test management tools such as Jira, Confluence and TestRail.
  • Updating tasks and project status.
  • Participating in QA and cross-functional team meetings.
  • Prioritizing test execution based on:
    • Business priorities
    • Defect patterns
    • Available testing timelines
  • Resolving challenges related to shared test environments and test data.
  • Participating actively in walkthroughs and defect triage sessions.
General & Soft Skills
The ideal candidate will demonstrate:
  • Proven technical leadership capabilities.
  • Ability to identify areas for improvement and recommend practical solutions.
  • Exceptional analytical, problem-solving and decision-making skills.
  • Strong verbal, written, interpersonal and presentation skills.
  • Strong troubleshooting and critical-thinking abilities.
  • Excellent listening and issue-resolution skills.
  • Strong consulting and stakeholder-management capabilities.
  • Proven ability to build effective relationships with technical and business stakeholders.
  • Excellent customer service, tact and diplomacy.
  • Ability to work effectively in a fast-paced, complex environment.
  • Strong organization, multitasking and time-management skills.
  • Flexibility, creativity, attention to detail and perseverance.
  • Proven ability to meet strict project deadlines.
Ideal Candidate Profile
We are looking for a senior/lead-level QA professional who combines deep systems testing expertise with strong public-sector healthcare experience, hands-on automation, API/web-service testing, SQL/data validation, accessibility testing, BI testing and defect management.
The strongest candidates will have demonstrated experience delivering QA/testing for large, complex and mission-critical healthcare systems within a public-sector environment and be comfortable working onsite with multidisciplinary project teams.
Important Submission Requirements
  • Only 1 candidate can be submitted.
  • The role is 100% onsite in Toronto at 5700 Yonge Street.
  • Standard schedule is Monday to Friday, 7.25 hours per day, between 8:00 AM and 5:00 PM, excluding lunch.
  • CRJMC security clearance is required.
  • 7+ years of senior QA/systems testing experience is required.
  • 5+ years of public-sector healthcare experience is required.
  • SQL/data-query experience is a specific MUST HAVE.
  • Candidates should demonstrate the mandatory healthcare, public-sector, testing, automation, API, security, accessibility, BI, SDLC, Agile/DevOps and defect-management experience directly in their resume.

title: Management Consultant - Associate
description:
You'll work in teams of typically 3 - 5 consultants to identify, and oftentimes implement, potential solutions for a specific client problem or challenge. Together, you will help clients make lasting improvements to their performance and realize their most important goals.

Over the course of each project, you will gather and analyze information, formulate and test hypotheses, and develop and communicate recommendations. You'll also present results to client management and implement recommendations in collaboration with client team members. In some cases, you will be asked to travel to your client site.

When you join McKinsey, you are joining a firm that will invest in your professional development. As an associate, you will receive training and coaching on how to better:

  • Structure ambiguous problems and take action to solve them
  • Synthesize clear takeaways from complex information into clear takeaways and recommendations using both qualitative and quantitative methods
  • Work effectively with diverse teams to come up with the best solution and move people and organizations to act
  • Establish trust-based relationships with clients to better serve their organizations
  • Communicate effectively with all audiences, including senior leaders, in a structured manner
  • Develop your leadership style, leveraging your own passions, strengths, and personal values

McKinsey believes in strengths-based development and coaching, and you’ll receive frequent mentoring from colleagues. This will include a senior colleague from your office or practice who will help you grow and achieve your career goals. Additionally, you will have a professional development manager who manages staffing to help you choose projects based on your priorities as well as the needs of client service teams.

While all consultants develop specialized knowledge as they progress with McKinsey, most are initially broad in their focus, meaning they do not need specific industry or functional expertise to be successful. For consultants who join McKinsey as experienced professionals, this can mean building on previous knowledge or developing experience in an area that is completely new.

QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor's degree; Advanced graduate degree (e.g., MBA, PhD, etc.) or equivalent (typically 5+ years) work experience preferred; Requirements may vary by country or practice
  • Ability to work collaboratively in a team and create an inclusive environment with people at all levels of an organization
  • Capability to drive an independent workstream in the context of a broader team project
  • Comfort with ambiguous, ever-changing situations
  • Ability to break down and solve problems through quantitative thinking and analysis
  • Ability to communicate effectively, both verbally and in writing, in English and local office language(s)

title: Post-Doctoral Research Associate
location: Edinburgh - Western General, Midlothian, United Kingdom
description:
UE07: £41,064 - £48,822 per annum

CMVM / Institute of Genetics and Cancer

Full-time: 35 hours a week

Fixed-term: 30 months


The Opportunity:

An exciting postdoctoral position is available to research the role of epigenetic marks in gene regulation.

We are looking for a self-motivated, enthusiastic postdoctoral research associate to join the laboratory of Dr Duncan Sproul at the University of Edinburgh’s Institute of Genetics and Cancer to understand the role of DNA methylation in gene regulation. This project is a close collaboration with 3 other groups based at the Universities of Edinburgh and Exeter.

We have recently characterised mutations that prevent the DNA methyltransferase DNMT3B from being recruited to actively transcribed gene bodies (Taglini et al. 2024, EMBO Reports 25:1130, DOI: 10.1038/s44319-024-00061-5). Our new project will use this knowledge combined with recently developed synthetic approaches as an entry point to probe the non-canonical regulation of transcription by DNA methylation within gene bodies and its functional impact on cellular phenotypes.

The successful candidate will work with the Sproul and collaborating laboratories as part of a successful multidisciplinary research team. This project will have a particular emphasis on the use of sequencing based functional genomics assays (eg TT-seq, CUT&RUN, Nanopore sequencing) in human embryonic stem cell models and work with synthetic landing-pad based approaches.

Candidates who have been awarded, or are soon to be awarded, a PhD in a relevant discipline and have experience with a broad range of molecular biology, cellular biology, biochemistry and/or computational data analysis approaches are invited to apply. Applicants must possess the ability to think independently while working within an interdisciplinary research team to drive research projects towards publication. Candidates with a strong track record in epigenomics, gene regulation and/or the use of human stem cells models are particularly welcome.

The post is full-time (35 hours per week) and funding is available from 1st January 2027 for 2.5 years pending review after 6 months.

Further details of work from the Sproul research group is available at:

Championing equality, diversity, and inclusion

The University of Edinburgh holds a Silver Athena SWAN award in recognition of our commitment to advance gender equality in higher education. We are members of the Race Equality Charter, and we are also Stonewall Scotland Diversity Champions, actively promoting LGBT equality.

Our key clients cover a wide range of different organisations in the private and public sectors. Key clients include financial institutions (pension funds, investors and financiers), operators (ports, rail, buses, highways and mobility) and wider industry.

The Advisory team is currently diversifying from a strong transport client base and has successfully developed its expertise into new sectors, namely industrial clients, major government programmes (e.g. Port Infrastructure Fund, UK Freeports) as well as mobility and core+ sectors.

We are regularly involved from project origination through to completion, as well as during asset optimisation and modernisation and/or expansion of existing facilities. Our front-end consultancy is supported by 60,000+ technical specialists globally. Our offer includes transaction services (including PPP), investment advisory, market studies, demand forecasting, technical and financial feasibility and management consultancy services.

What we will be looking for you to demonstrate…

  • A self-starting approach.
  • Ability to quickly synthesise large amounts of information and new concepts.
  • Degree level education in economics, engineering or similarly quantitative, analytical subject.
  • Being comfortable working with large datasets and/or programming languages such as Python or R and/or visualisation packages such as Power BI would be desirable.
  • An interest, or experience working across the transport, renewable energy and infrastructure sectors, in particular infrastructure investment.
  • A track record of working on financial and other analytical models for net zero, transport or infrastructure projects.
  • Knowledge of specialist modelling including scenario analysis or Monte Carlo analysis would be desired.
  • Experience working in a leading consultancy or other professional services firm.
  • Experience in delivery of workstreams or elements of workstreams to tight deadlines.
  • Ability to communicate your analysis in presentations and reporting to senior management audiences
  • Strong spoken and written communication skills in English is required and additional language skills would be desirable.
  • A comprehensive knowledge of all major relevant software packages (Word, Powerpoint etc.), and an expert in Excel with demonstrable knowledge of spreadsheet modelling best practice.

title: Lead Data Engineer – Microsoft Fabric
description:
Er du en erfaren data engineer, der brænder for at bygge robuste datapipelines og moderne dataplatforme og vil du være med til at forme, hvordan danske og nordiske virksomheder brugerMicrosoft Fabric? Vi søger en Lead Data Engineertil vores danske team. Niveauet afhænger af din erfaring og den rolle, du trives bedst i.

Om Evidi Decide

Evidi er et af Nordens ledende Microsoft-huse, ogDecideer vores data- og analyseområde. Vi hjælper kunder inden for en række sektorer med at gå fra data til indsigt – medMicrosoft Fabricsom kerneplatform. Vi er et nordisk team med kolleger i Norge og Danmark, der arbejder tæt sammen på tværs af projekter og landegrænser.

SomMicrosoft Solutions Partnermed specialisering inden forAnalytics on Azureer vi tæt på Microsoft og Fabric-fællesskabet. Vi tror på et stærkt fagmiljø, hvor viden deles gennem fagsamlinger, foredrag og løbende sparring.

Om rollen

SomSenior eller Lead Data Engineerbliver du en central del af vores leverancer til kunder, hvor du designer, bygger og videreudviklerdatapipelines og backend-dataplatforme. Det er det fundament, som god rapportering og AI-løsninger hviler på. Du er generalist: du tager dialogen med kunden og følger opgaven hele vejen til en færdig løsning – det kan være en dataplatform, en agent, en rapport eller noget derimellem.

Du vil typisk:

  • Designe, bygge og vedligeholdedatapipelinesog ETL/ELT-flows iMicrosoft Fabric(Lakehouse, Data Factory/Pipelines, Notebooks, OneLake)

  • Arbejde medmedallion-arkitektur, datakvalitet og governance på tværs af kundens dataplatform

  • Rådgive kunden om arkitektur og tekniske valg – du er lige så meget sparringspartner som udvikler

  • Samarbejde tæt med kunde og team – ofte som del af et mindre, tværfagligt leveranceteam

  • Arbejde på tværs af Fabric- og eventueltDatabricks-baserede løsninger, afhængigt af kundens platform

Som Senior Data Engineerer du det tekniske fyrtårn i leverancen. Du tager ejerskab for pipelines og datamodel, sikrer kvalitet og hjælper mindre erfarne kolleger med at lande gode løsninger.

Som Lead Data Engineertager du derudover det tekniske lederskab for leverancen. Du sætter arkitektur og retning, sikrer sammenhæng på tværs af teamet, coacher kolleger og er den, kunden læner sig op ad, når de store valg skal træffes.

Det forventer vi af dig

Fælles for begge niveauer:

  • StærkPythonog/ellerPySpark

  • Solid, praktisk erfaring medMicrosoft Fabric– eller et stærkt Azure-datastock (Synapse, Data Factory, Data Lake), som du kan bygge videre på i Fabric

  • Erfaring medbackend-dataarbejde: ingestion, transformation, orkestrering og datakvalitet

  • Evne til atrådgive og styre teknisk retningi projekter, gerne i en konsulentrolle

  • Gode kommunikationsevner på dansk og engelsk – du er komfortabel i dialogen med kunden

  • Arbejder med udgangspunkt iDanmark(med mulighed for opgaver på tværs af Norden)

Senior Data Engineer:

  • 5+ års erfaringmed datapipelines, ETL/ELT eller data engineering

  • Du tager selvstændigt ejerskab for tekniske leverancer og kan vejlede kolleger i det daglige

Lead Data Engineer:

  • 8+ års erfaringmed data engineering, herunder flere år med arkitektur og teknisk ledelse

  • Du har stået i spidsen for dataplatformsleverancer – sat retning, prioriteret og sikret, at teamet leverer

  • Du er vant til at coache andre data engineers og til at være kundens primære tekniske kontakt

Det er en fordel, hvis du har

  • Erfaring medAI-assisteret og agentisk udvikling– fx Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Claude Code eller lignende – og forstår, hvordan man giver god kontekst, verificerer output og arbejder sikkert med kundedata

  • Kendskab tilMicrosoft Foundryeller Azure OpenAI i data-/AI-workflows

  • Erfaring medDatabricks(Notebooks, Delta Lake, Unity Catalog, Jobs/Workflows)

  • Erfaring med migrering fra legacy BI/DWH til Fabric

  • Interesse forMCP, automatisering og moderne udviklingspraksis (Git, CI/CD for data)

  • Microsoft-certificeringer inden for Fabric, Azure Data eller Databricks

Hvad vi tilbyder

  • Et stærktnordisk data- og indsigtsmiljømed kolleger, der brænder for faget

  • Projekter hos spændende kunder inden for blandt andet offentlig sektor, finans og energi

  • Tæt partnerskab med Microsoft – adgang til nyeste teknologi, fagsamlinger og netværk

  • Reel mulighed for atpåvirke arkitektur og anbefalinger, ikke kun udføre opgaver

  • En arbejdsplads, hvorAI-værktøjer i det daglige arbejdeer en naturlig del af kulturen

  • Karrierevej mod arkitekt-, tech lead- eller rådgiverrolle – eller videre som Lead, hvis du kommer ind som Senior

title: Senior Research Associate, Antibody Discovery
description:
SystImmune is a leading and well-funded clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company located in Bothell, WA and Princeton, NJ. It specializes in developing innovative cancer treatments using its established drug development platforms, focusing on bi-specific, multi-specific antibodies, and antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs). SystImmune has multiple assets in various stages of clinical trials for solid tumor and hematologic indications. Alongside ongoing clinical trials. SystImmune has a robust preclinical pipeline of potential cancer therapeutics in the discover and IND-enabling stages, representing cutting-edge biologics development. We offer an opportunity for you to learn and grow while making significant contributions to the company's success.

We are seeking a highly skilled and motivated Senior Research Associate to join our Antibody Discovery Group. The successful candidate will play a critical role in supporting the discovery of novel antibodies for therapeutic development. This is a laboratory-based role that utilizes various techniques, including BCR amplification, sequence analysis, and recombinant antibody expression. This position offers an exciting opportunity to work in a dynamic and innovative environment focused on the development of novel therapeutic antibodies.

This is a full-time onsite position in Bothell, WA.



Key Responsibilities:

  • Amplify BCR sequences from sorted B-cells.
  • Select antibody candidates through BCR sequence analysis.
  • Design, clone, and express recombinant monoclonal antibodies.
  • Prepare detailed reports and presentations.
  • Maintain accurate records, ensure safety compliance, and contribute to lab organization.


Required Skills & Qualifications:

  • Bachelor or master’s degree in Immunology, Molecular Biology, Biochemistry, or a related field.
  • Senior Research Associate requires bachelor’s degree with 5+ years or master’s degree with 3+ years of industry experience.
  • 3+ years of hands-on experience in recombinant antibody expression.
  • Strong molecular biology background and experience.
  • Knowledge of antibody structure, humanization, production, and purification is preferred.
  • Hands-on experience in NGS library preparation and BCR repertoire analysis is a plus.
  • Experience in antibody discovery and development is highly desirable.

Technical Skills:

  • Highly proficient in molecular biology techniques, including PCR (general, nested, etc.), cloning, plasmid DNA isolation, RNA isolation, and sequencing.
  • Experience in eukaryotic cell transfection and culture.
  • Hands-on experience in humanization of antibodies using various methods.
  • Familiarity with sequence data analysis software and statistical tools (Geneious, Discovery Studio).

Soft Skills:

  • Effective communication skills, both written and verbal.
  • Strong organizational and time management skills.
  • Excellent problem-solving and troubleshooting abilities.
  • Ability to work independently and as part of a team.


Compensation and Benefits:

The expected base salary range for this position is $70,000 - $90,000 annually. Actual compensation will be based on a variety of factors, including but not limited to a candidate’s level qualifications, experience, and skills.

While most offers typically fall within the low to mid-point of the range, we may extend an offer toward the higher end for exceptional candidates whose background and expertise exceeds the requirements of the role.

SystImmune is a leading and well-funded biotech company with a bright future. We offer an opportunity for you to learn and grow while making significant contributions to the company’s success. SystImmune offers a comprehensive benefits package including: 100% paid employee premiums for medical/dental/vision, also STD, LTD, a 401(k) plan with a 50% company match of up to 3% and a vesting schedule of only 5 years, 15 PTO days per year, sick leave, plus 11 paid holidays and MORE.

We offer an opportunity for you to learn and grow while making significant contributions to the company’s success.

SystImmune is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We welcome diverse talent and encourage all qualified applicants to apply.

title: DevOps Team Lead
description:
DevOps Team Lead till Customer First

Om oss

På Customer First bygger vi nästa generations plattform för kundservice, med AI, automation och modern molninfrastruktur i centrum.

Vår plattform används varje dag av företag där tillgänglighet, prestanda och säkerhet är avgörande. Bakom den ligger en modern teknisk miljö med bland annat Kubernetes, GitOps, molninfrastruktur och distribuerade system.

Vi är idag över 30 personer och fortsätter växa. Nu söker vi en DevOps Team Lead som vill ta ett långsiktigt tekniskt ansvar för vår plattform och vara med och bygga upp nästa steg i vår DevOps-funktion.

Rollen

Det här är en roll för dig som fortfarande vill vara hands-on, men samtidigt vill ha möjlighet att påverka arkitektur, arbetssätt och tekniska vägval.

Du kommer arbeta nära utvecklingsteamet och ha en central roll i hur vi bygger, driver och vidareutvecklar vår infrastruktur. Fokus ligger på att skapa en stabil, skalbar och automatiserad plattform där vi kan växa snabbt utan att kompromissa med kvalitet eller tillgänglighet.

Initialt består DevOps-teamet av två personer. Ambitionen är att teamet ska växa över tid, och du kommer få möjlighet att sätta struktur, arbetssätt och teknisk riktning från början.

Du kommer bland annat att

  • Designa och vidareutveckla vår Kubernetes-plattform
  • Arbeta med skalbarhet, tillgänglighet och prestanda i produktion
  • Automatisera provisionering, deployment och drift
  • Vidareutveckla vår CI/CD- och GitOps-miljö
  • Arbeta med monitoring, logging och observability
  • Drifta och optimera SQL-databaser i större och hög­tillgängliga miljöer
  • Förbättra hur vi arbetar med incidenter, redundans och återställning
  • Ta tekniska beslut kring molninfrastruktur och plattformsarkitektur
  • Sätta standarder och best practices för DevOps tillsammans med utvecklingsteamet
  • På sikt vara med och rekrytera, coacha och utveckla DevOps-teamet


Vi tror att du har

  • Flera års erfarenhet av Docker och Kubernetes i produktion
  • God förståelse för Linux, nätverk och distribuerade system
  • Erfarenhet av CI/CD, exempelvis GitHub Actions
  • Erfarenhet av monitoring och observability med exempelvis Prometheus och Grafana
  • Erfarenhet av AWS, GCP, Azure eller motsvarande molnplattform
  • Erfarenhet av SQL-databaser i produktionsmiljö
  • Förmåga att felsöka komplexa problem och förstå hela kedjan från infrastruktur till applikation
  • Ett stort tekniskt intresse och vilja att förbättra, automatisera och förenkla


Du behöver inte ha varit chef tidigare. Det viktigaste är att du har den tekniska tyngden och viljan att ta ett större ansvar över tid.

Extra plus

Vi blir extra intresserade om du har erfarenhet av något av följande:

  • MySQL, MariaDB eller PostgreSQL i replikerade eller klustrade miljöer
  • Argo CD och GitOps
  • Terraform, OpenTofu eller annan Infrastructure as Code
  • Helm eller Kustomize
  • JavaScript/TypeScript, Go eller SQL
  • Kubernetes operators och stateful workloads
  • High availability och multi-zone-arkitektur
  • Att coacha andra tekniskt eller bygga upp ett team


Vad vi erbjuder

Hos oss får du inte bara förvalta en färdig plattform. Du får vara med och forma hur den ska se ut framåt.

Vi erbjuder:

  • Stor frihet att påverka teknik, arkitektur och arbetssätt
  • En central roll nära både produkt och utveckling
  • Modern infrastruktur och möjlighet att arbeta med teknik på riktigt i produktion
  • Korta beslutsvägar och stora möjligheter att få saker genomförda
  • Möjlighet att bygga upp och leda ett DevOps-team
  • Kompetenta kollegor och en miljö där teknik är en central del av verksamheten
  • Möjlighet till aktieoptioner för rätt person


Så jobbar vi

Vi tror på att de bästa tekniska lösningarna byggs när utveckling, produkt och infrastruktur arbetar nära varandra.

Därför arbetar vi tillsammans från vårt kontor i Stockholm, där du blir en naturlig del av utvecklingsteamet och kan påverka både stora arkitekturbeslut och det dagliga arbetet.

Vi söker dig som gillar kombinationen av teknisk spets, stort ansvar och möjligheten att faktiskt påverka hur saker byggs.

title: Foreman - Underground (Oncor)
description:
Position Summary

The Foreman is a safety focused professional with the ability to lead a crew to construct and repair electrical underground distribution systems. You will work on energized and de‑energized powerlines and may be required to travel to different job sites, including out‑of‑state locations, as operational and customer needs dictate. You will report to the General Foreman.

Essential Functions

  • Perform new construction, maintain and repair energized and de‑energized underground distribution systems while putting safety first.

  • Lead crew members and conduct pre-job and tailgate safety briefings.

  • Must be experienced with coaching and training lower classification employees in safe and productive work procedures.

  • Oversee work related to each project and assume full responsibility for its quality and completion deadline.

  • Install and repair underground facilities, underground conductors, including trouble shooting and fault locating on primary and secondary systems.

  • Comprehensive knowledge of switching and tagging procedures, grounding and induced voltage on energized and de-energized lines while using the proper tools and test equipment.

  • Understand how and when to obtain a one shot on a reclosing device.

  • Work in confined spaces, and in proximity to energized equipment.

  • Operate and maintain excavation equipment to include backhoes, trenchers, excavators, and pulling equipment.

  • Work outdoors in varying environmental conditions, including extreme heat, cold, rain, wind, and inclement weather.

  • Available to work outages, storms, emergencies including on call rotation.

  • Perform live‑line work using approved PPE and insulated sticks required for testing voltage and switching of energized lines.

  • Follow all safety protocols including PPE use and possess a comprehensive understanding of insulated protective cover to isolate differences of potential.

Minimum Requirements

  • Five (5) years of recent underground line experience.

  • Valid Commercial Driver's License (CDL).

  • Willing to travel long distances on short notice.

  • Lift, carry, push, or pull materials and equipment weighing up to 50 pounds.

  • Work for extended periods at job locations, including out‑of‑state assignments.

  • Willing to work outside of normal business hours, including weekends, holidays, emergency callouts, and overtime.

Physical Demands

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to perform the essential functions of this job.

While performing the responsibilities of this job, you will be required to talk, listen and use hand signals to communicate. The job frequently requires you to stand; walk; use hands and fingers to handle objects, operate tools or controls; reach with hands and arms.

Work Environment

While performing the responsibilities of this job, you are frequently exposed to fumes or airborne particles, moving mechanical parts and vibration. You are occasionally exposed to a variety of extreme conditions at constructions job sites. The noise level in the work environment and job sites can be loud. You will perform job responsibilities in extreme heat, cold, wet, windy, and storm conditions.

Our Benefits

  • Employee Assistance Program (EAP)

  • 401(k) with company match

  • Life insurance, and short-term and long-term disability

title: System Operator
description:
System Operator

Birmingham Alabama

The System Operator position is located at the Power Coordination Center (PCC) in Birmingham, AL which performs certain reliability functions set forth and strictly monitored by the North American Electric Reliability Corporation (NERC). The reliability functions include the Reliability Coordinator, Balancing Authority, Interchange Authority, Transmission Operator, and Transmission Service Provider. The System Operator position is based on progression, and entry points depend on the applicant’s relevant experience. Typical progression begins on the Interchange console, progresses next to the Balancing Authority console, and finally to the Reliability console. The successful candidate must demonstrate proficiency to assume roles at each operational console. Progression timelines vary between consoles; however, a System Operator will usually spend a minimum of 2 years on a console before progressing to the next.

There are three Consoles in the PCC where Operators work around the clock to manage the Southern Company BES. Below are the functional responsibilities of each console:

Interchange Console

- Utilize Open Access Same Time Information System (OASIS) to process hourly and daily requests for transmission service within the Southern Balancing Authority Area (SBAA)

- Process electronic tags (e-tags) for scheduling transmission service within the SBAA

- Make real-time changes to OASIS interface capacity offerings in the event of system constraints

- Manage scheduled power flows within or crossing the borders of the SBAA

- Perform hourly checkouts according to NERC with neighboring Balancing Authorities to verify incoming and outgoing scheduled transactions

- Perform hourly checkouts according to NERC with neighboring Balancing Areas to verify the amount of metered power across tie lines

Balancing Console

- Balance real-time generation and load within the Southern Balancing Authority Area

- Work in conjunction with Operations Planning and Generation Fleet Operations and to ensure that adequate generation is available

- Monitor generation reserves to handle unforeseen changes in load or system-to-system transfers

- Verify accurate metering of inter- and intra-company tie lines

- Develop day ahead and intra-day load forecast projections

Reliability Console

- Responsible for the safe and reliable operation of the Southeastern Sub-Region of the Southeastern Reliability

Corporation (SERC) including continuous monitoring of real-time system conditions

- Performs next day forecasting of system conditions to ensure that sufficient transmission and generation resources are available

- Configures resources such that the system will survive the single largest contingency

- Coordinate restoration efforts and resynchronize the grid in the event of a blackout condition

Candidates with the following preferred experience are encouraged to apply!

Education & Experience Requirements

- 3 + years of Electric Utility Transmission Operating experience and/or 5 + years of power plant operations experience highly desired

- Previous Electric Utility Transmission Operating experience as a Balancing Authority, Reliability Coordinator,

Transmission Operator and/or Interchange Authority is highly desired

- Control Center/Energy Management System (EMS) experience desired

-Previous experience/understanding working in energy/transmission markets is strongly desired

- College Degree preferred or equivalent work experience

- Previous experience working a rotating shift is a plus

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities

- Leadership and good interpersonal skills are required. The successful candidate will be expected to work with other professionals such as coordinators, operating company transmission control center personnel and management in a team-oriented and sometimes stressful environment

- Must be able to handle multiple tasks at one time, and be able to prioritize work and provide leadership during critical system events

- Must be comfortable with making decisions often with limited input and extreme time constraints

- Must have good problem-solving skills

- Must have comprehensive computer skills (including Excel and Word) to utilize numerous computer applications

- Broad knowledge of interconnected power system operations

- Excellent written and clear oral communication skills

- Working knowledge of Energy Management System (EMS) and its application/use in interconnected power system operations

Other Requirements

- Successful applicant is required to already have or obtain North American Electric Reliability Council (NERC) Reliability Coordinator operator certification, within 5 months of start date, before being able to perform operation duties and to facilitate continued employment. Training is provided to achieve such certification. While in training the successful candidate will report to the Operations Training Manager

-- The successful candidate will work a 24x7, 7-week rotating shift position - working 12-hour shifts including days, nights, and weekends (including holidays). See example below. Days/Nights are 12 hours, R’s (Relief Shift) are 8 hours, FX’s (Flex shift) are 8, and TF’s (Training Firm) are 10 hours. The schedule for the upcoming year is available before Thanksgiving and vacation is usually scheduled during the Relief weeks. Shift swaps and a vacation request process are utilized to facilitate vacation days for previously scheduled shifts.

Must pass EEI SO/PD II (System Operator/Power Dispatcher) test

Additional Testing Information

Candidates who meet the preferred hiring criteria will be invited to complete the SO/PD II Test. If selected, you will receive an invitation via email with further instructions. Please monitor your inbox (and spam/junk folder) for this communication.

Test Preparation Materials

To prepare for the SO/PD II Test, practice materials are available online. Please follow the steps below to access them:

Access the Practice Test

  1. Visit the EEI practice test website:
  2. Log in using the following credentials:
    • Username: southern
    • Password: testing
  3. Follow the on-screen instructions to locate and complete the SO/PD II practice test

Qualifications

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities

  • CSPDT - Certified Sterile Processing and Distribution Tech if hired in role on or after July 1, 2026 required

title: Director, Program Compliance
description:
The Opportunity:

The Ministry has an exciting opportunity for a collaborative leader for the permanent Director position (MCP 09).

The Program Compliance Branch leads investigative, enforcement and compliance activities for the new Immigration Services Act (ISA) and the Saskatchewan Immigrant Nominee Program (SINP). The ISA provides the most robust integrity framework for immigration in the country and the SINP supports Saskatchewan’s economic growth by attracting internationally trained workers to meet ongoing labour market demand.

The branch is responsible for administration of the ISA, which includes licensing of immigration consultants and recruiters and registering employers seeking to recruit international workers. The team leads investigations of potential violations of the ISA, misrepresentation or fraud by SINP applicants, employers, and nominees; auditing Immigration Services Branch file processing; and assessing areas of program risk. The Director will work with other ministries, governments and agencies involved in the enforcement of immigration legislation as well as all levels of law enforcement in the effective investigation and prosecution of violations of immigration law and the criminal code.

  • Administer and enforce the Immigration Services Act and Regulations.
  • Lead investigations and the preparation of disclosure packages.
  • Lead the development, enhancement and implementation of policies and procedures designed to uphold the integrity of Saskatchewan’s immigration system.
  • Establish collaborative and strategic relationships with other agencies and partners.
  • Implement a case management system that will reduce backlogs and provide a responsive service.
  • Develop an intake and referral process that is risk-based and triages appropriately.
  • Evaluate risk trends and develop risk mitigation strategies.
  • Lead, inspire and coach a diverse team to achieve client service excellence, innovation and continuous improvement, and a strong one-team approach.

Job Capabilities:

In this leadership and supervisory role, we are seeking someone who:

  • Holds themselves and others accountable for delivering on work expectations.
  • Demonstrates innovation and supports their team to identify, iterate, and implement new solutions.
  • Brings people together in a collaborative manner and builds relationships that deliver desired outcomes.
  • Is inclusive, promotes, supports, and enables belonging, encourages diversity, and values all contributions.
  • Is adaptable, anticipates the impact of change, models agility, and supports their team through ambiguity.
  • Is outcomes-focused, enables their team to meet or exceed established goals, and balances longer term objectives with tactical execution.

Technical Knowledge and Skills:

  • Education in investigation, criminal justice, criminology, or other related fields. Examples include law, sociology, accounting, computer science, or forensics.
  • Experience in investigations of fraud and misrepresentation especially related to identity and financial affairs of businesses and individuals and building cases for prosecution.
  • Experience in handling complaints in a program delivery context.

  • Experience designing and applying policies and procedures for a program that stand up to principles of procedural fairness and judicial review.

Job Skills:

  • Communication (Level D)
  • Critical Thinking (Level D)
  • Digital Skills (Level C)
  • Interacting with Others (Level D)
  • Navigating Ambiguity (Level D)
  • Managing Self (Level D)

  • Managing Organizational Resources (Level C)
  • Managing Talent (Level D)

Learn more about the Government of Saskatchewan’s Capabilities and Skills Framework here.

  • Comprehensive benefits package including pension
  • Vacation, scheduled days off, and other types of leave
  • Inclusive work environments
  • Career growth, development, and advancement opportunities

The Government of Saskatchewan upholds deep-rooted values of Respect and Integrity, Serving Citizens, Excellence and Innovation, and Acting as One Team.

description:

title: Leakage Detection Senior Operative - Cork County
description:
We are Uisce Éireann. Every day, we are responsible for the delivery of secure, safe, and sustainable water services for the people of Ireland. As Ireland’s national regulated water utility, our vision is a sustainable Ireland where water is respected and protected, for the planet and all the lives it supports.

Our purpose at Uisce Éireann is to rise to the challenge of delivering transformative water services that enable communities to thrive. That means we are proud to take on the responsibility of protecting our water supply and passing on a safe and secure water system to a rapidly growing population and empowering Ireland’s social and economic growth.

We are passionate about empowering our people, enabling them to make a positive impact on communities across Ireland. We are guided by a shared vision and purpose, grounded in values that define who we are and shape how we work, where we deliver for customers and communities, we work better together, we do the right thing, we aim high, and we keep each other safe. Our behaviours define how we interact, communicate, and succeed together. These values and behaviours apply to each one of us, across every role, location, and level.

Our goal is to attract and develop skilled and talented people from diverse backgrounds, who bring a dynamic range of expertise and insights to our work. With a strong, values-driven workforce, we ensure Uisce Éireann can continue advancing Ireland’s water services and meeting the needs of the communities we serve for generations to come.

The Role:

The Asset Operations function forms the cornerstone of service delivery to customers, protecting the environment and meeting regulatory standards as well as managing the majority of operational expenditure. The Asset Operations function has responsibility for operational and maintenance strategy, policies, planning and standard operating procedures for Water and Wastewater operations both nationally and regionally, ensuring that value for money and customer service is delivered.

The Operations and Management (O&M) team is responsible for the national delivery of water and wastewater operational services through the operation, inspection, maintenance & repair of the water and wastewater treatment and network assets.

Reporting to the Leakage Detection Team Lead, the Leakage Detection Senior Operative is responsible for monitoring Uisce Éireann pipe infrastructure using specialised equipment to measure water pressure and flow, detecting leaks in the network, and escalating these to the Team Lead.

Main Duties and Responsibilities:

  • Responsible for undertaking UFW reduction activities within the water network in order to deliver Uisce Éireann’s targets in relation to Water Conservation / Leakage Management.

  • Assisting with the maintenance of District Metered Areas (DMAs) including supervision of DMA meters to ensure correct configuration.
  • Responsible for carrying out leakage surveys and sweeps, pro-actively monitoring and checking the integrity and operability of District Meter Areas (DMAs).
  • Responsible for isolating and re-commissioning sections of the distribution network in a controlled manner so as to not adversely impact the network (alongside Water Network Operations teams) and carry out step testing and zero pressure testing activities.
  • Responsible for carrying out installation and monitoring of leakage detection equipment, including visual inspections of flowmeters and data-loggers, ancillary equipment and Pressure Reducing/Sustaining Valves (PRVs/PSVs).

  • Provide leadership for junior team members in driving the team’s performance culture

  • Support the collection and interpretation of data to identify areas of potential leakage - e.g. Flow and pressure monitoring, analysis of Nightline data, Night use allowances, DMA data, and data from the Leakage Management System (LMS), telemetry and customer metering databases.
  • Identifying if sources of UFW on the network are public or private side so that the most appropriate mechanism for effecting a repair can be identified. Responsible for engaging with private side customers as appropriate.
  • Responsible for temporary re-programming, deployment and collection of data from data-logging equipment for field tests.
  • Carry out inspections of electromagnetic, ultrasonic or mechanical bulk meters including identifying faulty equipment and raising work order for other teams (MEICA) to identify and repair specific faults.
  • Responsible for replacing battery packs on battery powered meters where appropriate.
  • Responsible for fully using handheld technology provided and carrying out associated training of this technology.
  • Responsible for adopting and fully using any new technology and carrying out associated training of this technology
  • Responsible for adhering to all HSQE plans, policies and procedures.
  • Ensure all health and safety procedures are adhered to and perform risk assessments (Safe System of Work Plan), use of PPE, etc.
  • Where assigned by the Leak Detection Team Lead, assist in establishing plans on how leakage sweeps and surveys will be undertaken.
  • Provides input into all processes and procedures affecting UFW management.
  • Identify errors or deficiencies in information to support UFW reduction activities contained within IW’s systems, i.e. GIS, LMS, Customer consumption databases, etc. and provide updated information gained as a result of their investigations to the appropriate team within Uisce Éireann.
  • Raise work orders for the repair of DMA infrastructure, such as ensuring the integrity of a DMA through boundary valve management or through the repair of faulty apparatus such as meters or logging equipment when this has been identified as part of any operability checks.
  • Maintain regular contact with Water Network Operations team on all aspects of network performance that may affect the UFW level within their area e.g. UFW triggers and pressures.
  • Assist the Customer Contact Centre with customer queries, as directed by the Leak Detection Team Lead. Assist the complaint resolution in relation to leakage control, water usage and pressures.
  • Responsible for collating data relating to the interventions required and providing information to the Leakage Detection Team Lead for approval.
  • Responsible for monitoring and reporting on KPIs over which they have ownership.
  • Participate in out of hours working as required.
  • Responsible for operating and maintaining Uisce Éireann vehicles and machinery, as required, in a responsible manner in line with all relevant Uisce Éireann vehicle, health, safety and security policies. Where the use of an Uisce Éireann vehicle is required, the following responsibilities will apply:
  • Reporting of road traffic accidents and near misses involving Uisce Éireann vehicles
  • Completing all required vehicle checks as set out by Uisce Éireann policies
  • Recording and reporting any vehicle defects to the Leak Detection Team Lead.
  • Responsible for ensuring stock levels in vehicles are sufficient for performing leak detection activities at first visit.
  • Providing assistance to Water Networks Operations, third party / contractors and internal customers in emergencies and on any areas relevant to effective UFW control as directed by the Leak Detection Team Lead.
  • Responsible for carrying out any other duties deemed necessary and / or required, which line management may reasonably request.

General Duties and Responsibilities

  • Collaboration with key internal stakeholders across the UÉ business.
  • Responsible for promoting and delivering health and safety commitments across UÉ and its supply chain, reinforcing positive behaviours and delivering health and safety objectives and requirements to the highest industry standards.
  • Support the delivery of the Uisce Éireann Transformation Programme, driving results required within the Directorate and supporting organisation-wide objectives.
  • Other duties as required.

Knowledge, Skills and Experience:

  • Secondary level education or equivalent work experience
  • A minimum of 2 years' relevant experience is required. Experience in a similar role in the water, utilities or similar industries would be an advantage
  • Full, clean and valid Irish category B driving licence is minimum requirement. Additional Driving License categories an advantage. A clean driving licence is defined as meaning that the applicant has not been convicted of an offence under the Road Traffic Acts (other than an offence for which the penalty is the imposition of penalty points).
  • We keep each other safe - experience and understanding of working within a strong health & safety culture
  • Ability to use monitoring and record-keeping IT equipment and interpret data and network drawings (GIS / Geo field) in order to analyse and investigate areas of potential interest in the network
  • Ability to trace and locate mains / services and street furniture to ensure access for leakage activities
  • Knowledge in the application of processes and procedures around proactive leakage detection and associated health and safety issues preferred
  • Ability to use leakage related IT equipment and interpret data and network drawings (GIS / Geo field) in order to analyse and investigate areas of potential leakage in District Metered Areas / Sub-District Metered Areas preferred
  • Ability to use leak noise correlators, acoustic sounding, data loggers, mechanical and/or electronic listening sticks, ground microphones and pressure and flow devices to interpret results and to pinpoint potential leakage. Required to understand the environmental factors that underpin the selection of the appropriate leakage techniques ad advantage
  • Thorough understanding of valve operations and of the operability issues associated with open boundary valves, incorrect DMA data and metering issues. Understand the processes and procedures relating to boundary valve auditing, tagging, tubing and boundary valve management.
  • Proactive, with ability to work on own initiative and with others to ensure success in the performance of a team
  • We work better together - proven ability to create and develop good working relationships to facilitate the accomplishment of work goals, coupled with the ability to gain commitment from others
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills with the ability to convey messages in a clear and concise manner
  • Ability to set up ongoing processes and procedures to collect and review information
  • Flexible with regard to working in a changing environment and the ability to adjust to new work structures, processes and requirements as necessary
  • We aim high - proactively identifying new areas of learning and using newly gained knowledge and skills on the job
  • Striving for quality and ensuring consistent high standards of work
  • Strong Computer skills with a proficient working knowledge of MS Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Outlook

The closing date for receipt of applications for this vacancy is 5th October 2026.

Please note that applications submitted after this closing date will not be accepted.

*Successful external candidates will be offered a salary within the advertised range based on an assessment of their relevant skills, qualifications, experience and readiness to undertake the responsibilities of the role.

Internal candidates will be considered in line with the application of Uisce Éireann's Pay Model and associated pay policies.

The salary range is designed to recognise that successful candidates may join the organisation at different stages in their career, while also providing scope for future salary progression as capability and experience develop.

Uisce Éireann is an equal opportunities employer.

We are committed to providing a diverse and inclusive place of work and have a robust strategy and framework called ibelong to enable this. We are an equal opportunity employer and through our recruitment process we welcome and encourage applications from interested and suitably qualified individuals regardless of gender, age, racial or ethnic origin, membership of the traveller community, religion or beliefs, family or civil status, sexual orientation/gender identity or disability.

title: Electrical Studies Engineer - Senior Level
description:

Tasks include the research, design, concept development, planning, and construction of transmission and distribution substations, power distribution, power regulation, renewable energy, as well as protection and control systems in a wide variety of contexts (utilities, transportation, building, and Federal, State, and local government projects). Provides situational guidance to PMs and managers that address current and future challenges, and that documentation and recommendations accurately account for and address risk, innovation, and future-ready opportunities.   • Actively oversee from project inception to completion, the management of design and construction of electrical infrastructure projects, including rehabilitation and reconstruction, site development, grading, drainage, equipment layout, elevations, specifications, building materials, phasing, and construction safety plans.

  • Meet with various public or private entities or individuals to discuss issues relating to a variety of electrical/engineering/construction challenges and programs.
  • Ensure technical reports and presentations explain research, findings, and recommendations to prevent, control, restore, or address electrical, design, and/or construction issues or opportunities.
  • Maintain a high level of quality and responsiveness to client requirements in alignment with Pickett’s standards.
  • Develop a client base for providing high level electrical engineering services including identifying additional business development opportunities.
  • Mentor staff to support their growth and professional development.
  • Remain current in latest electrical engineering techniques and practices.
  • Collaborates with professionals from a variety of disciplines, other engineers, planners, and infrastructure authorities on Federal, State, regional, and locally funded improvement and development projects, as well as proposal and business development opportunities.
  • Exercise responsible and ethical decision-making regarding company funds, resources and conduct, and adhere to WSP’s Code of Conduct and related policies and procedures.
  • Perform additional responsibilities as required by business needs.

Who You Are

Required Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s Degree in Electrical Engineering.
  • 10+ years of relevant post education experience as an electrical engineer providing design deliverables for capital projects in power generation, transmission, and distribution at a utility, industrial, or commercial scale.
  • Engineer license required (multi-state preferred).
  • Highly proficient with electrical engineering principles, practices, process, design/build, and the application to permitting and project work-related issues.
  • Highly proficient with infrastructure design.
  • Experience with infrastructure planning, design, and program/construction management; including comprehensive experience in working with adjacent disciplines such as electrical engineering, P&C, SCADA, and telecom.
  • Strong knowledge of relevant engineering and electrical construction laws, codes, regulations, compliance practices, and record-keeping requirements.
  • Highly proficient with making technical computations and calculations involving the application of engineering principles, understanding plans and specifications, and making factual comparisons to the appropriate regulations.
  • Experience with planning and conducting inspections and investigations on various aspects of the construction and design of facilities or structures, applying applicable regulations and policies
  • Highly effective interpersonal and communication skills when interacting with others, expressing intricate ideas effectively and professionally to an engineering and non-engineering audience.
  • Strong self-leadership and interpersonal communication skills with the ability to effectively, persuasively, and tactfully interact with clients, regulators, project managers, and employees at all levels of the organization.
  • Works independently to provide guidance and leadership to mid-level to senior level team or project members, with strict adherence to QA/QC.
  • Proficiency with technical writing, office automation, discipline-specific design software (i.e., CADD, Aspen, CAPE, ETAP, WIN IGS, Inventor, AutoCADD electrical), technology, math principles, predictive models, spreadsheets, and tools.
  • Experienced with providing critical review for documents and preparing technical deliverables and plans with a high degree of complexity.

description:
Become an integral part of the Corporate Responsibility (CR) team, working alongside dedicated professionals committed to generating authentic and durable social impact. The Corporate Responsibility (CR) Division leads the development and implementation of the firm's corporate responsibility strategy by setting goals, policies and initiatives that align with our business objectives, reflect our values, and strengthen the communities where we do business. The division includes Global Philanthropy, Public Engagement, Global Government Relations, the PolicyCenter, the JPMorgan Chase Institute, and Sustainable Finance.

The Global Philanthropy team is seeking a Vice President, based in Dallas, TX, to lead a philanthropic portfolio that advances economic opportunity as part of the U.S. Philanthropy team. As a Program Officer within Global Philanthropy, you will develop and execute strategies for the Dallas region. This includes designing and implementing philanthropic initiatives aligned with the firm’s business objectives, managing a grant portfolio, and building external relationships to advance strategic priorities. Competitive candidates will demonstrate deep knowledge of the Dallas market, credibility in the local community impact space, and established relationships with local partners and community networks. The Vice President will report to the Regional Executive for the U.S. South Region.

Job Responsibilities:

  • Collaborate with internal and external stakeholders to develop market strategies aligned with the firm’s business priorities and CR’s social impact agenda, including career and skills, small business and entrepreneurship, financial health, and affordable housing and community development

We are seeking an experienced Rail Operations and/or Maintenance professional to play a key role in growing our CEAS presence across the Republic of Ireland and Northern Ireland. This pivotal role will act as the primary CEAS/Rail Advisory point of contact for our Irish rail clients, helping shape, win, and deliver high quality advisory, operational and technical services across both jurisdictions.


A little more about your role...
We’re looking for skilled and experienced Chartered Engineers with a strong background in railway maintenance to join our Rail Asset Management & Maintenance team, part of WSP in the UK’s Rail Advisory group. Our work involves supporting our clients across the full asset lifecycle, from strategy development and design analysis through to operations, renewals, and continuous improvement. With a focus on safety, maintainability, cost-efficiency, and asset performance, we help organisations realise the full value of their assets, working to best practice and standards such as ISO 55000, ISO 55001, and ISO 55002.

This is a varied role, blending rail maintenance advisory, asset management, and high-level consulting applied to a range of rail disciplines including rail systems and infrastructure, digital signalling systems and rolling stock. On some projects you’ll be deep in the detail resolving operational issues; on others you’ll be shaping strategic, organisational, and operational change. Our work spans operational system specifications, design reviews, whole-life cost analysis, asset & organisational resilience to climate change, maintenance planning, maintainability and accessibility assessments and the development of asset management strategies and systems. We integrate new and complex technologies into whole-system solutions, ensuring that they deliver lasting value for our clients.

We are a client-facing, problem-solving team that thrives on collaboration. Often embedded within client organisations, we work closely to understand their challenges and co-create practical, future-ready solutions. Our mix of practical and technical expertise, organisational understanding and strategic insight means we’re often called in to troubleshoot difficult or high-profile projects. We are equally comfortable operating at the strategic, executive level as we are at the practical and tactical level getting hands when required.

With flexible UK locations and occasional international travel, you’ll join a team that values entrepreneurial thinking, fresh ideas, and a sharp eye for opportunities, helping to future-proof rail operations and act as a strategic enabler for our clients.

title: Lead Credit Officer
description:
Join Business Banking Risk as a Lead Credit Officer and play a key role in supporting growth within JPMorgan Chase's Government and Not-for-Profit portfolio. This position combines independent credit authority, transaction structuring, and risk management, offering the opportunity to evaluate complex lending opportunities, partner with business leaders, and help drive sound credit decisions that support clients while protecting the firm.

As a Lead Credit Officer Vice President within Business Banking Risk, you will be responsible for the oversight, management and credit decisioning of new and existing extensions of credit for the Business Banking line of business. Responsibilities include analysis of credit opportunities, structuring transactions, negotiating and reviewing terms, identifying risks, conducting due diligence, and applying credit authority.

Job Responsibilities:

  • Exercise independent credit authority to evaluate, structure, and approve Business Banking credit transactions while ensuring alignment with firm risk appetite, underwriting standards, and policy requirements.
  • Serve as a trusted risk advisor to Relationship Managers and business partners, balancing growth objectives with prudent risk management through thoughtful transaction structuring, including terms, covenants, collateral, and other risk mitigants.
  • Underwrite and manage credit exposures within the Government and Not-for-Profit sectors, performing comprehensive due diligence through financial analysis, cash flow assessment, evaluation of industry and sector dynamics, and qualitative assessment of management and organizational strength.
  • Synthesize financial, operational, industry, and borrower-specific information to identify material risks, assess repayment capacity, and formulate well-supported credit recommendations and approval decisions.
  • Identify, escalate, and drive resolution of material credit concerns, portfolio trends, or emerging risk issues that may impact asset quality or portfolio performance.
  • Ensure appropriate risk grading, documentation, and decision rationale while maintaining audit-ready records and adherence to regulatory and internal requirements.
  • Contribute to a strong risk culture by sharing expertise, coaching colleagues, and promoting consistent underwriting and credit risk management practices.


Required Qualifications, Capabilities, and Skills:

  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent professional experience.
  • Minimum 5 years experience in Credit Risk, Loan Credit, or similar subject.
  • Demonstrated experience evaluating, structuring, and approving commercial credit transactions, with the ability to exercise independent judgment and articulate clear, evidence-based credit decisions.
  • Strong understanding of credit risk management principles, including financial analysis, risk identification, transaction structuring, risk grading, and portfolio management concepts.
  • Proven ability to assess complex borrower situations, balance business objectives with risk considerations, and recommend practical risk mitigation strategies.
  • Executive-level written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to influence stakeholders, negotiate transaction structures, and present clear recommendations to business and risk leaders.
  • Strong organizational and prioritization skills, with the ability to manage a diverse portfolio of work in a fast-paced, highly regulated environment.


Preferred Qualifications, Capabilities, and Skills

  • Experience supporting Government, Municipal, and/or Not-for-Profit clients, including familiarity with sector-specific credit considerations and underwriting approaches.
  • Demonstrated success managing complex credit relationships and transaction structures involving customized covenant, collateral, or repayment arrangements.
  • Experience serving as a trusted advisor, coach, or mentor to credit professionals and business partners.
  • Advanced degree in business, finance, accounting, or a related discipline.

To be eligible for this role, you must be authorized to work in the United States. We do not offer any type of employment-based immigration sponsorship for this role. Likewise, JPMorgan Chase & Co. will not provide any assistance or sign any documentation in support of any other form of immigration sponsorship or benefit, including optional practical training (OPT) or curricular practical training (CPT).

description:

Consulting keeps us close to the hardest real-world problems. Products let us solve them at scale. Every engagement sharpens our products; every deployment makes the next engagement faster, deeper, and more certain.

We're obsessed with outcomes. While 95% of enterprise AI pilots never reach production, Visium is built to be the 5% delivering productised AI that compounds in value, not point solutions that deliver marginal gains. We are AI-native, not AI-adjacent. We don't bolt AI onto broken workflows; we redesign them with AI at the core.

  • 8+ years of experience in AI, Data, Digital Strategy, Management Consulting, or a related field, with significant experience leading complex strategy engagements.
  • Proven track record of developing and executing AI & Data strategies from vision and roadmap through implementation and value realization.
  • Strong understanding of AI/ML, GenAI, data platforms, and emerging AI technologies, with the ability to translate technical concepts into business value.
  • Strong strategic and analytical abilities, with creative problem-solving on complex issues.
