title: Junior DevOps Engineer
description:
We are hiring a hands-on Junior DevOps Engineer to join our infrastructure team and build reliable, scalable systems on top of our own bare metal stack. You will be working on real infrastructure that powers a production platform 1,500+ automotive dealerships across Europe.

You will work directly with our DevOps Tech Lead to build the platform that empowers our developers to self-serve.

The Mission: Platform Engineering

We are Autoflows. We serve 1,500+ automotive dealerships across Europe, and our platform is the "nervous system" of their aftersales service. When we work, they make money. When we stop, they stop.

Unlike many SaaS companies, we are profitable. We don't rely on the next VC round to pay salaries; we rely on our product's commercial success. We are looking for a Junior DevOps Engineer who understands that shipping features pays the bills.

  • Infrastructure as Code, Done Right: We are replacing manual, one-off server configurations with proper IaC using Terraform and Ansible. Every change is tracked, every environment is reproducible.
  • Developer Self-Service: We build pipelines and tooling that let developers ship confidently and independently, without needing to involve infrastructure for every deployment.
  • Pragmatic by Design: We run on Hetzner bare metal (EU). We default to open-source solutions on our own hardware, but we are not dogmatic – we use managed services where they genuinely save time and reduce risk.

Our Technical Focus

We Have Clear Goals For The Coming Year. We Are Not Chasing Every New Trend; We Are Building a Solid Foundation. Our Tech Lead Owns These Areas – You Will Contribute And Learn

  • Core Infrastructure: Maturing our Proxmox clusters and implementing a robust, segmented network architecture.
  • Data Platform: Supporting our data infrastructure work around Airflow and Medallion Architecture.
  • Future PoCs: We are exploring Kubernetes and Kafka at a proof-of-concept level.

Engineering Compliance

Compliance Is Something We Take Seriously, But We Solve It With Engineering Rather Than Paperwork. As a Junior, You Will Be Exposed To This Work And Contribute Under Guidance. You Will Help Us

  • Test Environments: Help maintain and improve our test environments so they mirror production safely, without exposing real customer data.
  • Access Management: Support our access management setup (Keycloak) and learn how our GitOps workflows serve as an automated audit trail.
  • Security Hardening: Contribute to network segmentation and firewall configuration via IaC, learning how infrastructure can be made secure by design.

What You Will Actually Do (The Day-to-Day)

  • Infrastructure as Code (IaC, learning on the job): You will write the Terraform and Ansible code that replaces manual server configurations.
  • Virtualization & Networking: You will manage Proxmox clusters and Linux environments. You will help improve our network setup, moving towards secure, segmented, and observable subnets.
  • Postgres Operations: Support our Senior DevOps in operating our self-managed PostgreSQL clusters. You will learn backup verification, basic tuning, and how to keep a production database healthy.
  • Developer Support: You will support our product teams. You don't need to write app code, but you need to understand their architecture and build pipelines to help them ship.
  • Identity & Access: You will support our access management setup, learning how authentication flows work and helping ensure the right people have the right access.

What You Bring To The Table

  • Linux Fundamentals: You are comfortable navigating Linux systems from the command line. You understand processes, permissions, filesystems, and basic networking.
  • Scripting & Automation: You know at least one scripting or programming language (Bash, Python, or similar) and you use it to automate repetitive tasks rather than doing them by hand.
  • Curiosity & Drive: You are eager to learn, ask questions, and get things done. You are not afraid to dig into unfamiliar tools or systems.
  • Pragmatic Mindset: You can accept "good enough" when the situation calls for it. You understand that perfect is the enemy of done in a fast-moving product company.
  • Team Player: You genuinely like helping people, whether that means supporting a developer with a pipeline issue or jumping in during an incident.
  • Ops Mentality: You are drawn to Ops work. You find satisfaction in systems that just work, and you take ownership when they don’t. You are more SysAdmin at heart than Developer.
  • Works Well Under Pressure: Things break in production. You stay calm, communicate clearly, and focus on resolution.
  • Comfortable asking for help and sharing what you learn – we grow as a team.

Ideally, you also have

  • Some networking experience (even basic knowledge of VLANs, firewalls, or routing).
  • Exposure to virtualization technologies (Proxmox, VMware, or similar).
  • Some exposure to containers (Docker, Podman) or basic Kubernetes concepts. We are exploring this space and it’s useful context.
  • Familiarity with CI/CD tools such as GitLab, GitHub Actions, Jenkins, or Azure DevOps.
  • A home lab or personal projects. We love people who tinker on their own time.

Note: This role is fully onsite in our Copenhagen office (Højbro Plads).

About our interview process

  • Online or face-to-face introduction to Autoflows and you (30 minutes)
  • Case-based interview + general knowledge with team members and CTO (1 hour)
  • Closing talk with CEO including compensation, starting date, and all other practical details (30 minutes)

About Us & The Team

Autoflows is a profitable, high-growth scale-up (~60M DKK ARR) and a highly international team of 55 employees. Our offices are located on Højbro Plads in the vibrant Matrikel 1 startup community.

We have an informal and relaxed atmosphere with team events, breakfasts, and Friday bars. Our work culture is built on four key values: Proactivity, Curiosity, Ownership, and Collaboration. We are customer-centric and focused on delivering best-in‑class solutions while constantly learning.

title: Data Governance Senior Associate
description:
Your expertise in data governance can make a real difference — join a team where the work you do directly strengthens the integrity of information that drives decisions across JPMorganChase.

As a Data Governance Senior Associate at JPMorganChase, you will play a central role in ensuring that critical data is well-defined, accurately documented, and ready for use across Compliance, Finance, Risk, and Controls. You will partner with Data Owners, Technology, and governance teams to maintain high-quality metadata, support data quality processes, and help resolve issues that impact downstream data consumers. This is an opportunity to contribute to a culture of data excellence within a firm that values precision, accountability, and continuous improvement.

Job responsibilities

  • Document, publish, and maintain metadata including business names, definitions, source application details, and governance attributes to ensure data consumers can understand and trust critical data assets
  • Partner with aligned Data Owners to support metadata quality, clarify data management expectations, and reinforce governance accountability across the organization
  • Support end-to-end governance of data elements and datasets, including intake triage, completeness review, documentation, approval workflows, and publication readiness
  • Assist with Data Quality rule writing, monitoring, testing, validation, and effectiveness reviews to ensure rules accurately reflect business intent and control requirements
  • Research and support remediation of data quality issues, tracking open items, documenting outcomes, and driving appropriate closure actions in partnership with relevant teams
  • Maintain awareness of downstream data usage across Compliance, Finance, Risk, and Controls to ensure governance activities align with business and regulatory needs
  • Review metadata quality reporting, identify improvement opportunities, and recommend actions to reduce rework and strengthen governance outcomes
  • Communicate clearly and proactively with Data Owners and partner teams regarding governance priorities, issue status, and required actions

Required qualifications, capabilities, and skills

  • Formal training or certification on data engineering concepts and 3+ years applied experience
  • Demonstrated ability to translate business context into clear metadata definitions, governance documentation, and data standards
  • Strong stakeholder partnership skills with the ability to collaborate effectively across business, technology, product, data quality, and control functions
  • Comfort reviewing and interpreting operational metrics, data quality rules, issue trends, and rule logic
  • Strong written communication skills with exceptional attention to detail, follow-through, and the ability to manage multiple concurrent priorities
  • Ability to work independently, escalate appropriately, and drive tasks to completion in a complex, matrixed environment

Preferred qualifications, capabilities, and skills

  • Familiarity with enterprise data governance frameworks, data cataloging tools, or metadata management platforms
  • Experience supporting data governance programs within financial services, risk, compliance, or regulatory environments
  • Exposure to data lineage, data classification, or critical data element programs
  • Experience working with cross-functional teams including Chief Data Office, Finance, Risk, or Compliance functions
  • Knowledge of data quality rule design, issue management workflows, or governance intake processes

title: Project Manager- Demolition Engineering
description:
Bring your curiosity and determination to make a meaningful impact on complex infrastructure and facilities projects supporting Canada’s defence and industrial sectors.

Join a global professional services leader committed to solving the world’s biggest challenges in water, energy, and urbanization. At GHD, we deliver integrated engineering, advisory, and project management services that improve the physical, natural, and social environments of the communities in which we operate.

We offer a collaborative and technically focused environment grounded in our core values of Safety, Teamwork, Respect, and Integrity, with ongoing professional development through GHD Business School.

Who are we looking for?

Our Property and Building team is growing, and we are seeking a Project Manager to lead the delivery of complex, multidisciplinary facilities and infrastructure projects. This role is based in Ottawa, with flexibility to work from any of our GTA offices.

This position requires a balance of project leadership and technical oversight, with a strong focus on design integration, delivery execution, and client advisory.

Working within our Decommissioning & Demolition team, you will

  • Support and help grow our team in Ontario while working on a diverse range of clients and engineering projects including demolition and building renovation projects throughout Canada
  • Act as the project manager for existing and future demolition and closure projects
  • Actively participate in business development initiatives to help grow our business in the Ontario market
  • Supervise and coordinate multi-discipline project teams
  • Produce design calculations and contribute to the formulation of design concepts and technical specifications
  • Assist in quantity take-off and cost estimating assignments
  • Deliver and be accountable for technical assignments
  • Lead the preparation of tenders and proposals
  • Participate in field investigations including material take-offs, existing conditions assessments and sampling for hazardous materials
  • Develop your decision-making, communication and technical skills

What you will bring to the team

  • Minimum of 3-6 years experience in the consulting or construction industry
  • A real passion for problem solving
  • An organised approach to meeting deadlines
  • The ability to collaborate and be an adaptable team member
  • Adaptability and a flexible approach to working across a variety of projects
  • Excellent written and verbal communication
  • Building engineering, demolition experience and/or estimating experience is advantageous
  • Relevant tertiary qualification

Please note:

  • The salary range for this position is $78,000 to $110,000. The posted salary range represents the expected hiring range for GHD locations in its major city centres. Ranges may vary for positions in other locations. At GHD, base salary is determined by your skills, experience, qualifications and work location. We are committed to offering competitive compensation and adhere to all relevant pay transparency legislation.

  • The use of artificial intelligence (AI) in recruiting is just getting started and may be used during the process to improve efficiency and fairness. Your application may be reviewed by both AI and our hiring team. While AI supports some steps through the process, all final hiring decisions are made by humans

  • This position is for an existing vacancy

As a diverse and inclusive organization, we encourage individual achievement and recognize the strength of a diverse workforce. GHD is an equal opportunity employer. title: Operational Technology Infrastructure Engineer/Consultant
description:
At Sword, we help power, secure and transform the organisations that keep the UK running. Supporting customers across Critical National Infrastructure, energy, public sector and enterprise markets, we combine deep industry expertise with leading technology services spanning managed services, cyber security, cloud, data, AI and digital transformation.

Join Sword and you'll be part of a team solving complex challenges, delivering real-world impact and working alongside talented colleagues who care deeply about quality, collaboration and customer success.

About the Role:

  • Design, build and configure VMware environments.
  • Build and configure physical and virtual server environments.
  • Support Windows and Linux-based infrastructure platforms.
  • Support the hosting and deployment of OT and industrial applications.
  • Support application installation, configuration, integration and infrastructure readiness.
  • Undertake system, application and infrastructure testing and validation prior to deployment.
  • Support FAT, SAT, commissioning and production go-live activities.
  • Support infrastructure migrations, upgrades and refresh programmes.
  • Configure Active Directory, Group Policy, DNS and supporting infrastructure services.
  • Implement resilient, highly available infrastructure for critical OT systems.
  • Support storage, backup, recovery and disaster recovery solutions.
  • Undertake infrastructure health checks, troubleshooting and performance analysis.
  • Support server hardening, patching and vulnerability remediation.

  • Work alongside OT, cyber security, network, application and engineering teams.

Requirements

  • Strong experience with Windows Server build, configuration and administration.
  • Experience with Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL) or equivalent Linux platforms.
  • Experience with physical and virtual server deployment.
  • Experience supporting application hosting and application infrastructure.
  • Experience with system testing, validation and acceptance activities.
  • Active Directory, Group Policy, DNS and DHCP.
  • High availability, clustering and infrastructure resilience.
  • Enterprise server hardware including Dell, HPE or equivalent.
  • SAN, NAS and enterprise storage technologies.
  • Backup and disaster recovery technologies
  • Good understanding of networking, VLANs, firewalls and segmentation.
  • Server hardening, patching and lifecycle management.
  • Experience producing technical infrastructure and test documentation.
  • Experience within OT, industrial, energy, utilities or CNI environments would be highly desirable.
  • Knowledge of IEC 62443, NCSC CAF or OT cyber security principles would be advantageous.

title: Power & Energy Project Manager
description:
This Opportunity

WSP is seeking a Power & Energy Project Manager for our Power & Energy Program Management Office in Lakewood, CO.

This position provides high level technical project leadership, and guidance with managing the administrative, commercial, and technical components of Power Generation project(s) or portfolio of projects in accordance with WSP’s core values, and the level of project services agreed upon in the contract by WSP and the client(s). Responsible for the overall performance of assigned project(s) that are moderate and larger size/complexity and regional in scope, and includes oversight for financial, technical, client satisfaction, quality, safety, and schedule. Ensures responsibilities throughout the project lifecycle (proposal phase, planning and project startup, project execution, reporting, and project closeout) are adhered to, delivered, and audited with a level of quality that meets or exceeds corporate project excellence and delivery standards. Provides innovation, administration, and pragmatic direction to address current and future project management challenges in a rapidly changing and complex business and operations climate.

Your Impact

  • Provide PM leadership for larger scale/more complex projects ensuring contributors know what they are required to do and by when, preparing and overseeing relevant project budgets, forecasts, margins and KPIs, monitoring external events and risk contingencies, tracking hours and expenses, ensuring satisfactory performance, and managing the contractual obligations to deliver the project or assigned portfolio of assigned project(s) as defined in the contract.
  • Lead the development of project proposals, cost estimates, scope, schedules, and resource plans
  • Oversee management of budgeting, forecasting, scheduling, cost and change management and control.
  • Participate in the technical aspects of contract negotiation, presentations, and meetings.
  • Provide regular project reporting and updates to clients, technical leads, and business leaders, identifying any emergent issues with scope, risk, and/or budget and mitigation strategies.
  • Be the face of WSP for the client. Develop and nurture strong, long-term relationships with client by understanding their needs, providing tailored solutions, and ensuring consistent communication to drive satisfaction and retention.
  • Mentor staff to support their growth and professional development.
  • Adherence to proven processes and ability to develop new processes to standardize procedures.
  • Adhere to safety regulations and enforce project safety standards
  • This position is subject to and contingent upon client approval of candidates put forth for consideration by WSP
  • Exercise responsible and ethical decision-making regarding company funds, resources, and conduct, and adhere to WSP’s Code of Conduct and related policies and procedures
  • Perform additional responsibilities as required by business needs.

Who You Are

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree (Electrical, Civil, Mechanical, Project Management or Construction Management), Engineering Technology, Physical Sciences, or a related technical discipline, or equivalent professional experience within an A/E/C firm, utility, EPC, or power delivery consulting environment.
  • 12+ years of relevant post education experience in a project management role within our industry.
  • Highly proficient understanding of project delivery process and strong background and experience in project management. Experience managing projects through a variety of delivery models (DBB, EPC, PDB).
  • Advanced proficiency with analytical and organizational skills, with business acumen to bridge the business and project management.
  • Advanced proficiency with interpersonal and communication skills to interact effectively, persuasively, and tactfully with leadership, subcontractors, and employees at all levels of the organization.
  • Excellent self-leadership with attention to detail, multi-tasking, and adjusting readily to the changing prioritization of responsibilities in a dynamic work environment.
  • Works independently and provides guidance and leadership to mid-level to senior level team or project members, with strict adherence to QA/QC.
  • Advanced proficiency with technical writing, office automation, relevant software, MS Office suite products (e.g., Word, Excel, Visio, Project, SharePoint), technology, spreadsheets, and PM tools.
  • Ability to elicit cooperation from a wide variety of sources, including senior management, subcontractors, consultants, and company-wide staff, including those with whom no formal hierarchical relationship exists.
  • Strong ability to quickly adapt to change and demonstrate flexibility to a variety of schedules and hours to meet project-specific needs.
  • Proven track record of upholding workplace safety and ability to abide by WSP’s health, safety and drug/alcohol and harassment policies.

WSP Benefits:

WSP provides a comprehensive suite of benefits focused on providing health and financial stability throughout the employee’s career. These benefits include coverage related to medical, dental, vision, disability, and life; retirement savings; paid sick leave; paid vacation (or other personal time); paid parental leave; and paid time off for purposes of bereavement, voting, and/or attendance at naturalization proceedings.

Compensation:

Expected Salary (Colorado only): $130,300 - $230,000

WSP USA is providing the compensation range that the company in good faith believes it might pay and/or offer for this position within the state of Colorado, based on the successful applicant’s education, experience, knowledge, skills, and abilities in addition to internal equity and specific geographic location. WSP USA reserves the right to ultimately pay more or less than the posted range and offer additional benefits and other compensation, depending on circumstances not related to an applicant’s sex or other status protected by local, state, and/or federal law.

title: Football Laundry Student Worker (WS-ST1)
description:
Job Title: Football Laundry Student Worker (WS-ST1)

Classification: Student Employee (non-exempt)

Name and Address of Employer: St. Olaf College, 1520 St. Olaf Ave, Northfield, MN 55057

If the position requires the student to work off campus, provide the name and address here:


Department Name: Football

Unit Number (5 digits): 11707

Length of Position: See Employment Authorization

Contact Person/Supervisor: Head Football Coach

Wage Range: $12.00-13.00/hour


Description of the Position: (Purpose of the Position):

The Football Laundry Worker is an essential member of the St. Olaf Football support staff. This position is responsible for washing, drying, folding, and organizing all laundry associated with the football program, including daily practice laundry loops, towels, workout gear, and full game uniforms.

Each player has a laundry loop that contains their practice clothing; these loops must be washed, dried, and returned to the correct locker promptly. Towels are collected, washed, and folded daily. After each game—home or away—game uniforms must be collected, washed separately, dried or hung properly, and placed back in the equipment room in an organized manner.

You will be fully trained on how to operate washers and dryers, including which settings are appropriate for towels, loops, game uniforms, and specialty items. Proper laundry care helps maintain the quality of our equipment and ensures our team is prepared to practice and compete at a high level.

This position requires responsibility, reliability, and attention to detail. Laundry must be completed in a timely manner—including late nights after home and away games when the team returns to campus and uniforms need immediate washing.



Transferable Skills:

Working in this role develops several important skills that translate directly into everyday life, future employment, and leadership responsibilities:

Responsibility and Ownership

  • Workers learn to take full responsibility for completing essential tasks that impact the entire football program.

Time Management and Dependability

  • Laundry has strict deadlines—especially after games. Learning to manage time and stay on task builds strong habits.

Attention to Detail

  • Sorting items, using correct washer settings, and returning items to the proper place require focus and accuracy.

Work Ethic & Follow-Through

  • Staying late after games or managing high laundry volume teaches dedication and the importance of finishing a job the right way.

Task Management

  • Workers learn how to organize workflow, prioritize tasks, and complete multiple steps in a consistent system.

Care for Equipment & Materials

  • Proper handling of uniforms and towels teaches respect for gear and reinforces professionalism.

Teamwork & Communication

  • Communicating with the equipment staff and coaches ensures that the team’s needs are met and that laundry is completed correctly.



Duties and Responsibilities:

Daily Practice Laundry

  • Collect players’ laundry loops after practice.

  • Wash loops using the correct washer settings.

  • Dry loops thoroughly and return them to each player’s locker.

  • Wash and fold all towels used during practice.

  • Maintain a clean and organized laundry area.

Game Day Laundry

  • Collect game uniforms immediately after home games.

  • For away games, wash uniforms as soon as the team returns to campus—even late at night when necessary.

  • Wash game uniforms separately and with the correct settings to avoid damage.

  • Hang uniforms in the equipment room according to the program’s organizational system.

  • Ensure everything is completed and ready for the next day’s activities.

Equipment Care & Proper Handling

  • Use washer/dryer settings correctly for towels, loops, practice gear, and game uniforms.

  • Treat all uniforms and equipment with care—these items are costly and must be maintained properly.

  • Report any damaged equipment or laundry issues to the equipment room staff immediately.

Professional Expectations

  • Arrive on time and complete all assigned shifts.

  • Stay until all laundry is finished—even if it requires late hours after games.

  • Work efficiently and stay on task during busy laundry times.

  • Keep laundry areas clean, organized, and safe.

  • Maintain team confidentiality and respect the equipment room environment.



Qualifications: (Education/Experience/Skills) No prior experience required.

Physical and Environmental Factors:

This position requires crouching, stooping, twisting/pivoting, grasping/handling, pushing/pulling, lifting and carrying objects up to 50 lbs., and operating equipment to perform the essential functions. It also requires exposure to odors, chemicals, and wet or humid conditions indoors. Candidates must possess the ability to safely perform the physical work required of all duties with or without reasonable accommodation.


This job description is for general information purposes. It is not intended to list all duties and responsibilities of the position. This job description is subject to change at any time by St. Olaf College, with or without prior notice.

title: Executive Director - Technology Risk & Controls (IAM)
description:
Executive Director - Technology Risk & Controls (IAM)

Join JPMorganChase's Identity & Access Management (IAM) organization as an Executive Director within Technology Risk & Controls. This leadership role is responsible for advancing technology risk management, control effectiveness, audit readiness, and continuous control monitoring across a critical portfolio supporting the firm's security and identity capabilities.

The successful candidate will lead strategic initiatives focused on strengthening the design, execution, and sustainability of technology controls while driving modernization efforts across risk, governance, and audit processes. This role requires strong expertise in artificial intelligence (AI), data management, audit response modernization, and continuous control management to support the firm's evolving risk landscape and regulatory expectations.

Job Responsibilities

  • Lead the development and execution of technology risk and control strategies across IAM.
  • Drive continuous improvement of control effectiveness, control coverage, and risk transparency.
  • Sets reuse-first expectations for enterprise-authorized AI adoption within the work environment across technology risk and controls operations to accelerate evidence synthesis, issue analysis, and executive reporting, with human-in-the-loop validation and appropriate handling of sensitive data.
  • Modernize audit and regulatory response processes through automation, data-driven insights, and AI-enabled capabilities.
  • Establish and enhance continuous control monitoring frameworks to improve risk identification, reporting, and remediation.
  • Partner with technology, cybersecurity, product, operations, compliance, audit, and control organizations to strengthen governance and control outcomes.
  • Leverage data management and analytical capabilities to improve control measurement, reporting, and decision-making.
  • Provide executive-level reporting and risk insights to senior technology and business leadership.
  • Support strategic initiatives involving AI governance, operational resilience, risk management, and regulatory readiness.
  • Lead and develop a high-performing team of risk, control, and governance professionals.
  • Establishes governance standards for AI-assisted workflows used in risk reporting and issue/action-plan management, ensuring traceability/auditability and alignment to security, resiliency, and regulatory expectations.

Required Qualifications

  • 7+ years of experience in technology risk management, cybersecurity, or a related field, focusing on regulatory compliance and risk mitigation (NAMR/APAC – India/ LATAM/Hong Kong)
  • Demonstrated experience leading safe adoption of enterprise-authorized AI capabilities within the work environment within technology risk and controls workflows, including validation practices and awareness of data sensitivity.
  • Ability to define review/approval and escalation expectations for AI-assisted recommendations while maintaining security, auditability, and regulatory compliance outcomes.
  • Significant experience in technology risk management, controls, audit, cybersecurity, identity and access management, or related disciplines.
  • Demonstrated success leading large-scale risk and control transformation initiatives.
  • Experience working with internal audit, external audit, regulatory examinations, and remediation programs.
  • Strong understanding of technology control frameworks, governance practices, and control monitoring techniques.
  • Experience applying data management, analytics, automation, and AI capabilities to improve risk and control outcomes.
  • Exceptional executive communication and stakeholder management skills.
  • Proven ability to influence senior leaders and drive cross-functional execution.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience in Identity & Access Management (IAM), Privileged Access Management (PAM), cybersecurity controls, or enterprise technology governance.
  • Experience developing continuous control monitoring, metrics, telemetry, and risk reporting capabilities.
  • Knowledge of AI governance, data governance, and emerging technology risk management practices.
  • Experience leading regulatory, SOX, SOC, or enterprise control programs.

title: Senior Backend Developer
description:
We are looking for a Senior Backend Developer to help build the best digital assistant for professional kitchens.

Running a profitable and enjoyable foodservice business - without sacrificing chef creativity - is incredibly hard. FoodOp is on a mission to change that globally.

More than 700 chefs across 550+ kitchens use FoodOp daily to manage recipes, menus, procurement, and reporting—and we’re just getting started.

You will join our development team in Copenhagen, working closely with frontend and backend developers, as well as designers.

About The Role

This is a hands-on engineering role. You’ll spend most of your time designing and building product alongside the rest of the team.

You Will

  • Own substantial backend features from product discussions and data modelling through implementation and deployment
  • Help evolve our backend architecture, scalability, and reliability as the product grows
  • Make pragmatic technical decisions that balance shipping today with building for tomorrow
  • Contribute to backend patterns and engineering practices across our Python applications
  • Participate actively in code reviews and technical discussions
  • Work closely with frontend engineers, designers, and customers to build great product experiences and public APIs

What We’re Looking For

We care more about what you’ve built and the environments you’ve worked in than your exact number of years of experience or previous titles.

We think you’ll be a great fit if you:

  • Have 4+ years of professional backend development experience
  • Are a strong, hands-on engineer who enjoys building and owning software in production
  • Have strong fundamentals in data modelling, APIs, databases, backend architecture, reliability, and maintainability
  • Have good technical judgment - knowing when to move quickly and when foundational work will pay off
  • Can independently take an ambiguous problem, understand the product need, explore the tradeoffs, and ship a solution
  • Enjoy technical discussions and can both challenge and be challenged without ego
  • Have strong product sense and care about what we build, not just how we build it

We’re particularly interested if you’ve been part of a startup or engineering team through a period of significant growth. You’ve seen technical decisions that aged well, some that didn’t, and learned what becomes important as a product and team scale.

You don’t need to have been the architect or technical lead—we care about what you learned from the experience.

We primarily use Python, but deep Python experience is less important than being an excellent backend engineer.

Ways of Working

We’re a small, talent-dense team that values ownership, high velocity, and low-ego collaboration. Everyone takes responsibility for the codebase. Decisions are made through dialogue and alignment, and we value curiosity, continuous learning, and thoughtful problem-solving

As a Senior Backend Developer, you’ll take responsibility for backend quality, architecture, and best practices, while mentoring and guiding other developers. You’ll make a real impact on a critical part of the product and help shape how the team works.

Our team works to high technical standards and actively uses AI tools to prototype, explore, and ship faster.

Tech Stack

  • Backend: Python (Flask)
  • Databases: Postgres, Elasticsearch, Redis
  • DevOps & tooling: Docker, Helm, K9s
  • Cloud & infrastructure: Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS)
  • Messaging & real-time: WebSockets
  • APIs: RESTful services
  • Version control & CI/CD: Git and GitLab pipelines
  • Frontend: Angular and TypeScript

title: Senior, Sorter

I. Job Summary

The Sorter is responsible for ensuring proper placement and sorting materials on the conveyor line by performing the following duties.

  • Pull contaminants out of paper or off of floor.
  • Stack boxes and skids. Dump boxes and totes of material.
  • Feed material, such as wastepaper onto conveyor.
  • Clean up conveyor and surrounding sorting line. Keep surrounding work area clean.
  • Read monitor for machine start up and ensure machine is operating properly and at a moderate speed.
  • Follow appropriate standard operating procedures (SOPs) as guideline for operating and maintaining equipment.
  • Report any worker-public safety factors and/or equipment malfunctions.
  • Attend weekly/monthly safety/operations meetings.

title: Bar Supervisor
description:

title: 2027 Markets Quantitative Trading & Research Associate Program – Off-Cycle Internship - Hong Kong
description:
Quantitative Trading & Research (QTR) is an expert quantitative modeling group in J.P. Morgan, as well as a leader in financial engineering, data analytics, statistical modeling and portfolio management. We’re looking for innovative problem-solvers who enjoy building complex solutions that support global business.

Over the duration of 3 - 6 months, you’ll build mathematical models and tools, gain exposure to risk modeling and investment banking, and develop through hands-on projects, mentorship, and a speaker series.

Based on your individual achievements, those who successfully complete the program may receive offers of full-time employment.

Job Responsibilities

  • As an associate in Quantitative Trading & Research (QTR), you will get exposure across Derivatives Pricing, Risk Management & Electronic Execution and Systematic, Data-Driven Trading Analytics teams that drive innovation and process optimization using machine learning (e.g., collaborative filtering, deep learning, reinforcement learning) across sales/client engagement, risk, portfolio optimization, and electronic trading/market making.
  • Partner with traders, marketers, and risk managers across products and regions to promote sales, client interaction, product innovation, valuation, and risk management.
  • Develop and implement mathematical models for pricing, hedging, and risk measurement of derivative securities, as well as models for algorithmic and Delta-One strategies and inventory management.
  • Support both OTC and electronic trading activities by explaining model behavior, identifying major sources of risk in portfolios, carrying out scenario analyses, developing and delivering quantitative tools, and researching new trading ideas. .
  • Assess the appropriateness and limitations of quantitative models, monitor associated model risk, and implement valuation, risk, and trading models in production systems.
  • Design efficient numerical algorithms and implementing high performance computing solutions; design and develop software frameworks for analytics and their delivery to systems and applications.
  • You will apply machine learning and other advanced analytics to enhance sales and client engagement, risk management, portfolio optimization, and electronic trading and market making.
  • Contribute to business outcomes and client franchise; identify revenue opportunities; develop market intuition, including cross-asset impacts.
  • You will apply advanced analytics to pricing, hedging, and idea generation; research medium to high-frequency trading strategies; develop portfolio construction methods and new systematic modeling approaches.

Required qualifications, capabilities and skills:

  • Expected graduation beyond December 2027
  • Currently pursuing a Master’s in a quantitative field (e.g., Mathematics, Physics, Engineering, Computer Science, Machine Learning, Statistics)
  • Proficiency in at least one programming language (e.g., Python, Java, JavaScript, C++, C#)
  • You demonstrate quantitative and problem-solving skills as well as research ability
  • You are good at communicating concepts and ideas, both verbally and via documentation, and explain technical concepts to non-technical audiences

Preferred qualifications, capabilities and skills:

  • Understanding of advanced mathematics arising in financial modelling (probability theory, stochastic calculus, partial differential equations, numerical analysis, optimization, machine learning, statistics, econometrics…)
  • Knowledge of options pricing theory, trading algorithms or financial regulations
  • Beyond that, we’re interested in the things that make you unique: personal qualities, outside interests and achievements beyond academia and profession
  • Candidates requiring visa sponsorship may apply

Application Deadline

29 November (23:59 Hong Kong time)

Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis. We strongly encourage you to submit your application as early as possible as programs will close once positions are filled.

Join us

At JPMorgan Chase, we’re creating positive change for the diverse communities we serve. We do this by championing your innovative ideas through a supportive culture that helps you every step of the way as you build your career. title: Laitoshuoltaja Jorvin sairaala
description:
Haluatko olla mukana tekemässä merkityksellistä työtä sairaalan puhtaanapidon tehtävissä?

Haemme laitoshuoltajia 2-vuorotyöhön Jorvin sairaalaan toistaiseksi voimassa oleviin työsuhteisiin.

HUSin tukipalvelut, viralliselta nimeltään Runkopalvelut, vastaa siitä, että sairaalassa on parhaat mahdolliset puitteet potilaiden hoitamiseksi.

Meillä laitoshuoltajan tehtävät ja työympäristöt ovat monipuolisia ja vaihtelevia. Pääset osaavan ja mukavan tiimisi kanssa varmistamaan, että tilat ovat puhtaat, turvalliset ja viihtyisät sekä asiakkaille että henkilökunnalle. Lisäksi tehtäviisi voi kuulua myös ruokahuollon avustavia tehtäviä, vuodehuoltoa ja muita huoltopalvelutehtäviä.

Työpaikan sijainti: Jorvin sairaala, Espoo

Työsuhde: vakituinen, kokoaikainen, 2-vuorotyö

Työehtosopimus ja palkkaus: SOTE-sopimus, tehtäväkohtainen 2473,91€/kk ja sopimuksen mukaiset lisät

Työn aloitus: 30.9.2026 tai sopimuksen mukaan

Tässä videossa pääset tutustumaan laitoshuoltajan työhön: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vmJH8yR0878

Miksi töihin HUSin Runkopalveluihin?

  • Monipuolisissa potilaan hoitoa tukevissa tehtävissä olet tärkeä osa sairaalamaailmaa.
  • Kattava perehdytys: kukaan ei joudu kylmiltään työntekoon. Saat myös aina apua perehdytyksen jälkeenkin.
  • Rento ja monimuotoinen työyhteisö, johon jokaisen työntekijän on helppoa tulla mukaan. Meillä kaikki auttavat toisiaan parhaansa mukaan ja töitä tehdään yhdessä hyvällä fiiliksellä.
  • Monipuoliset ura- ja koulutusmahdollisuudet, esimerkiksi mahdollisuuksien mukaan koulutus palvelutyöntekijän tehtäviin.
  • Työterveyshuolto, liikunta-, kulttuuri- ja työsuhdematkaetu, tuettu työpaikkaruokailu sekä vaihtuvia henkilökuntaetuja liikunta- ja hyvinvointipalveluista.

Mitä toivomme sinulta?

Ilahdumme hyvistä vuorovaikutustaidoista ja iloisesta palveluasenteesta, sillä teet töitä tiiviisti työkavereidesi kanssa asiakkaidemme hyvinvoinnin eteen. Lisäksi toivomme ammattimaista ja reipasta työotetta, koska työ on vaihtelevaa ja jokainen työpäivä voi olla erilainen.

Suomen kielen suullinen ja kirjallinen taito on välttämätön.

Näin haet

Lähetä hakemus sähköisellä hakulomakkeella hakuajan loppuun mennessä. Voimme aloittaa haastattelut jo hakuaikana.

HUSissa olet osa vaikuttavinta hoitoa.

Tehtävän kelpoisuusehdot

Laitoshuoltajan tai toimitilahuoltajan tutkinto.

Kelpoisten ja tehtävään soveltuvien hakijoiden puuttuessa työnantaja voi palkata määräajaksi henkilön, jolla on riittävä kokemus alalta.

Edellytämme asiakas- ja potilastiloissa työskentelevältä tartuntatautilain mukaista rokotussuojaa, ja terveydenhuollon toimintayksiköissä työskentelevältä terveydentilan selvitystä keuhkotuberkuloosista ja salmonellasta.

Tehtävään valittavan tulee olla täysi-ikäinen.

Yhteystiedot

Lisätietoja tehtävästä antaa arkisin palveluesihenkilö Jenny Uitto puh. 050 428 4879 tai jenny.uitto@hus.fi

title: Building Maintenance Tech I - Full Time, Days
description:
This position typically starts at $18 per hour and works a variable schedule, including evenings, weekends and holidays. Team members begin accruing PTO starting on day one, and full‑time employees are eligible for benefits after 90 days.

Entry level facilities maintenance. Independently performs skilled preventive maintenance, troubleshooting, repair, and installation work across multiple building trades. Resolves moderately complex equipment and facility issues, documents corrective actions, supports projects and vendors, and provides practical guidance to less-experienced technicians.

  • Complete assigned preventive maintenance and basic inspections in accordance with established schedules, checklists, manufacturer guidance, and department procedures.

  • Perform routine repairs involving doors, locks, hardware, furniture, walls, ceilings, flooring, fixtures, signage, and other building components.

  • Assist with basic plumbing tasks such as repairing or replacing faucets, flush valves, supply lines, traps, fixtures, and clearing minor drain obstructions within authorized scope.

  • Assist with basic electrical tasks such as replacing lamps, approved fixtures, switches, receptacles, and related components within training, licensing, and safety limitations.

  • Perform painting, patching, caulking, minor carpentry, assembly, moving, installation, and general property upkeep assignments.

  • Respond promptly and professionally to work orders and service requests from guests and departments; communicate status and escalate unresolved or unsafe conditions

  • Inspect assigned areas for leaks, damage, trip hazards, unusual sounds or odors, lighting concerns, deterioration, and other deficiencies.

  • Use the computerized maintenance management system or approved work-order process to document labor, materials, observations, and completion details accurately.

  • Prepare work areas, protect adjacent finishes, post required signage or barriers, and restore areas to a clean and operational condition after work is complete.

  • Maintain assigned tools, carts, equipment, parts, and workspaces in safe, clean, and serviceable condition.

  • Assist higher-level technicians, contractors, and department leadership with repairs, projects, shutdowns, emergencies, and special events.

  • Provide courteous service and minimize disruption to gaming, hotel, food and beverage, entertainment, and administrative operations.

  • Comply with all company policies, safety rules, internal controls, emergency procedures, and applicable federal, state, local, and gaming regulatory requirements.

  • Maintain any required gaming license, registration, work permit, driver qualification, or other property-specific credential as a condition of employment.

  • Immediately report unsafe conditions, injuries, security concerns, compliance issues, equipment failures, and suspected hazards through established channels.

  • Protect confidential information and safeguard property assets, keys, tools, materials, and access credentials.

  • High school diploma or GED required.
  • Up to 2 years of maintenance, construction, hotel engineering, apartment maintenance, or related experience preferred.
  • Basic knowledge of hand and power tools, repair techniques, and computer/mobile applications.
  • Valid driver's license may be required.
  • Trade school training, safety certifications, or experience in a 24/7 commercial environment are a plus.
  • Basic understanding of building maintenance systems and safety practices.
  • Ability to troubleshoot issues, prioritize tasks, and work independently.
  • Strong communication, customer service, teamwork, and attention to detail.
  • Ability to follow instructions, complete documentation, and maintain reliable attendance.
  • Ability to stand, walk, bend, climb, and lift up to 50 pounds.
  • Comfortable working indoors and outdoors, at heights, in confined spaces, and around mechanical equipment.
  • Ability to use personal protective equipment and communicate effectively by phone or radio.
  • Work is performed throughout a casino, hotel, and entertainment facility.
  • Schedule may include nights, weekends, holidays, overtime, and on-call assignments.
  • Must obtain and maintain any required licenses, certifications, permits, or gaming credentials.
  • Must meet company requirements for background screening, drug testing, and driving eligibility, when applicable.
  • Complete work safely, accurately, and on time.
  • Maintain clear documentation and communication.
  • Demonstrate professionalism, teamwork, and respect for company assets and guests.

description:

Nesta área você terá uma visão transversal dos negócios de Químicos da Braskem, além de ter interfaces com diversas áreas como: Produção, Comercial, Logística, Matérias Primas, Energia, Performance Industrial, etc.

O principal desafio é ser protagonista no ciclo de planejamento de produção, estocagem e vendas dos principais petroquímicos do sudeste.

Principais atividades a serem realizadas:

Definir e direcionar ciclo S&OP e S&OE de maneira integrada, viabilizando os melhores ajustes operacionais para a maximização dos resultados da organização.

Conduzir e direcionar as decisões do ciclo S&OP, viabilizando a maximização dos resultados da empresa.

- Discutir e alinhar as premissas para compor o S&OP – Coleta de dados, Planejamento de Matéria Prima e Planejamento de Demanda e de Produção.

- Definir o plano ótimo de produção – Planejamento de Produção e Vendas (nível tático)

- Planejar e divulgar a execução operacional do ciclo – Agendamento de Produção (nível operacional)

Tratar as mudanças dos cenários ao longo do mês – S&OE, de forma a ajustar o plano ótimo de produção à realidade.

- Conduzir e tomar decisão durante as discussões de S&OE junto as áreas Industriais, Comerciais e Logísticas.

- Qualificar os desvios das operações e as justificativas pertinentes ao alcance da aderência do ciclo S&OP.

Requisitos para a vaga (conhecimentos específicos)

- Graduação de Química, Engenharia Química ou Engenharia de Produção;

- Excel Avançado;

- Inglês intermediário (desejável);

- Conhecimento de Power BI e/ou Data Analytics (diferencial).

Perfil da vaga

Forte senso de autodesenvolvimento, proatividade, espírito de equipe, bom relacionamento interpessoal, capacidade de síntese, análise e foco.

title: Private Client Banker- Princeton Branch - New Jersey Princeton Market
description:
You have a passion for taking care of our customers and employees and making them feel welcomed and valued by building lasting relationships, doing the right thing, exceeding expectations and having a strong commitment to diversity and inclusion. Here at Chase, you will have the opportunity to help people experience our Customer Promise -- helping people make the most of their money so they can make the most of their lives by providing education and advice tailored to suit their financial needs.

As a Private Client Banker in Branch Banking, you are the main point of contact for a select group of Chase’s affluent clients as well as other customers in the Branch. You will manage their complete banking relationship across the company, utilizing a proactive and disciplined approach to generate growth in their balances. You will help acquire new clients by actively soliciting referrals and developing internal and external sources.

Job responsibilities

  • Shares the value of Chase Private Client with clients that may be eligible
  • Actively manages their banking relationship through an advice-based approach, ensuring each client receives the best products and services for their needs
  • Partners with Specialists (Private Client Advisors, Mortgage Bankers and Business Relationship Managers) to connect customers to experts who can help them with specialized financial needs
  • Makes lives of clients more convenient by sharing and setting up self-service options to access their accounts 24 hours a day/ 7 days a week
  • Adheres to policies, procedures, and regulatory banking requirements

Required qualifications, capabilities, and skills

  • Demonstrated success using a value-added, relationship-oriented approach to acquire and deepen client relationships
  • 1+ year Branch Banking Banker or equivalent experience in financial services, with verifiable success in new client acquisition, cultivating, and maintaining customer relationships and revenue generation
  • Beginning Oct. 1, 2018, if you are not currently registered, the Securities Industry Essential (SIE) exam, FINRA Series 6/7, state registration (including 63 or 66 if required) and Life licenses are required - or must be successfully completed within 180 days of starting the role
  • Compliance with Dodd Frank/Truth in Lending Act*
  • High school degree, GED, or foreign equivalent
  • Adherence to policies, procedures, and regulatory banking requirements
  • Ability to work branch hours, including weekends and some evenings

Preferred qualifications, capabilities, and skills

  • Excellent communication skills
  • College degree or military equivalent
  • Experience cultivating relationships with affluent clients
  • Strong team orientation with a commitment of long-term career with the firm

Dodd Frank/Truth in Lending Act

This position is subject to the Dodd Frank/Truth in Lending Act qualification requirements for Loan Originators. As such, an employment offer for this position is contingent on JPMC's review of your criminal conviction history, credit report, information available through NMLS, and any other information relevant to a determination by JPMC that you demonstrate financial responsibility, good character, and general fitness for the position. Note that any felony conviction within the last seven years will disqualify you from consideration for this position. Your continued employment in this position would be contingent upon compliance with Truth in Lending Act/Dodd Frank Loan Originator requirements.

In addition, this position requires National Mortgage Licensing System and Registry (NMLS) registration under the SAFE Act of 2008. As such, upon active employment with JPMorgan Chase, you will be required to either register on NMLS, or to update your existing registration as necessary to grant access to and reflect your employment with JPMorgan Chase. Your continued employment in this position with JPMorgan Chase is contingent upon compliance with the SAFE Act, including successful registration immediately after your start date, and timely completion of annual renewal and required updates thereafter.

Any information obtained during the registration, update, and renewal processes or through NMLS notifications may impact your employment with the firm. Any of the completed information you provide during the Chase on-line application process may be transferred, on your behalf, to NMLS by JPMorgan Chase. Please carefully review the information you provide to Chase for accuracy and consistency and with any current NMLS record, if applicable, before submitting. Under the direction of the Membership Experience Manager, the Donor Relations Associate, Passport and Ambassador is primarily responsible for supporting KQED’s higher level Membership programs as well as helping coordinate one of its most popular membership benefits, Passport.

title: Crew Leader - Underground (Preco)
description:
Position Summary: The Underground Crew Leader position is a skilled position in the construction, maintenance and repair of electrical underground distribution systems.

Essential Functions:

  • Work safely while performing new construction, maintenance or repair work of energized and de-energized underground work.
  • Supervises crew members.
  • Possesses working knowledge of leadership and management skills.
  • Capable of leading and training lower skilled employees in safe and productive work procedures.
  • Capable of leading and teaching underground services, infrastructure and duct banks.
  • Conducts pre-job or tailgate briefings.
  • Possess a working knowledge of all aspects of underground distribution.
  • Troubleshoots problems on underground circuit.
  • Frequently works with energized high voltage systems requiring skill and care to protect the lives of themselves and others.
  • Maintains company vehicles, equipment and tools in good working order.
  • Comply with company reporting procedures and complete required company paperwork.
  • Coordinates and inspects the work of crew members.
  • Able to perform rigorous physical labor.
  • Able to identify primary and secondary voltage on a circuit.
  • Must be familiar with induced voltage.
  • Possesses knowledge of tools for terminating cable.
  • Understands grounding procedures.
  • Understands how to obtain a one shot on a reclosure.
  • Capable of working in confined spaces.
  • Capable of properly installing and removing PPE and cover up.
  • Understands grounding procedures.
  • Capable of testing and classifying soil.
  • Understands how to safely operate equipment.
  • Understands how to phase out a line using phasing sticks.
  • Capable of planning safe work based on a job print or work order.
  • Understands sloping and shoring requirements.
  • Possesses a working knowledge of ladder requirements.
  • Able to properly ask for and take line clearances.
  • Possesses a working knowledge of line protection devices.
  • Able to properly inspect rubber goods and PPE.
  • Able to identify and locate puller and tensioner setups.
  • Does all other related work as required to complete the job.

Other Requirements:

  • Able to travel long distances on short notice, when required.
  • Understands flag and tag procedures.
  • Possesses a CDL and demonstrates safe driving.
  • Able to work for extended periods in various locations, when required.
  • Able to lift in excess of 50 lbs.
  • Must be able to work outside, frequently in inclement weather.
  • Willing to work over-time when requested.
  • Willing to work outside of the normal work schedule including weekends, holidays, and overtime as required for the position.

Physical Demands:
The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job.
While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to talk or hear. The employee is frequently required to stand; walk; use hands to finger, handle, and feel; and reach with hands and arms.

Work Environment:
While performing the duties of this job, the employee is frequently exposed to fumes or airborne particles, moving mechanical parts and vibration. The employee is occasionally exposed to a variety of extreme conditions at construction job sites. The noise level in the work environment and job sites can be loud. This position is performed in outside weather conditions.

Competencies:

  • Self-Motivated
  • Team-Oriented
  • Customer Oriented
  • Must be able to follow Company safety rules and all other Company policies.

NOTE: This job description is not intended to be all-inclusive. Employee may perform other related duties as required to meet the ongoing needs of the organization.

title: Investment Banking [Multiple Positions Available]
description:
DESCRIPTION:

Duties: Analyze detailed corporate and financial information to develop meaningful insights. Create statistical exhibits and models that analyze comparative financial performance. Build models that illustrate projected financial results and value to companies. Define, guide, and review detailed valuation analysis, including DCF, trading comparables, transaction comparables, and LBO analyses. Define, guide, and review detailed combination and other financial analyses in the context of M&A transactions or pitch situations. Lead due diligence and drafting sessions. Take on select client coverage responsibilities. Proactively generate ideas for clients and exploit trends in industry, product, and competition. Develop strong internal and external networks and effectively leverage firm resources. Prepare and manage the delivery of internal deal memos, engagement letters, and internal processes across deal execution and management. Create an efficient workflow, and translate overall direction into clear roles and responsibilities. Assume responsibility for the various phases of project and transaction execution, new business development, and overall growth of the firm. Develop a strong understanding and knowledge of technology, software, and sub-sectors of the software industry, the companies therein, competitive dynamics, capital market perspectives on the sector. Develop content for strategic meetings with clients regarding M&A or capital market transactions. Interact with Directors at the firm and client management teams on a daily basis to execute transactions and discuss strategic alternatives. Develop marketing materials and participate in delivery of client presentations. Draft private and public marketing materials such as offering memoranda, confidential information memoranda, and SEC legal documents. Provide leadership, mentorship, and supervision to Associates and Analysts. Proactively attract, develop, and retain top talent by participating in undergraduate and graduate recruiting. This position requires up to 30% domestic travel to JPMC sites.

QUALIFICATIONS:

Minimum education and experience required: Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Finance or related field of study plus four (4) years of experience in the job offered or as Investment Banking, Analyst, Consultant or related occupation. The employer will alternatively accept a Master’s degree in Business Administration, Finance or related field of study plus two (2) years of experience in the job offered or as Investment Banking, Analyst, Consultant or related occupation.

Skills Required: This position requires two (2) years of experience with the following: Financial modeling and analyses pertaining to both U.S. and cross-border Mergers & Acquisitions (M&A) including building detailed financial operating models, 3-statement combination and divestiture models, discounted cash flow valuations, present value of future stock prices, precedent transactions, trading comparables, LBO analyses, intrinsic and market-based value creation analysis, and accretion and dilution analyses; M&A transactions including acquisition and sale of both U.S. and non-U.S. private and public companies; Divestiture of a division, spin-off, Reverse Morris Trusts, and related corporate restructuring; Financial restructuring transactions including representing sellers and buyers in section 363 sales processes under the bankruptcy code; Transactions involving PE funds and both cash and stock consideration; Conducting fairness opinion analyses for clients, including related procedures and drafting proxy disclosures; U.S. or cross-border M&A transactions in an investment bank within several sections; Corporate defense assignments against activist investors; Financial statement analysis and due diligence for buy-side and sell-side M&A transactions including distressed M&A, negotiating with stakeholders including creditors of distressed businesses, and transaction structuring; FactSet for market data and analysis.

Job Location: 270 Park Avenue New York, NY 10017. This position requires up to 30% domestic travel to JPMC sites.

Full-Time. Salary: $260,000.00-$285,000.00 per year.

I. Job Summary

The Plant Associate will ensure all waste is unloaded from vehicles, the vehicles are decontaminated, and waste is properly staged for scanning and processing. The individual will perform the duties in a safe and productive manner.

  • Unload waste from incoming vehicles. Separates non-autoclavable waste to be incinerated.
  • Stage waste on conveyor system or properly stack waste for scanning in the Biotrack system.
  • Scan waste into the Biotrack system for proper recordkeeping purposes.
  • Load autoclave bins or incinerator hopper with waste for processing.
  • Place reusable containers on tub wash line for decontamination.
  • Operates tub wash unit ensuring the wash unit is operating properly. Removes clean tubs from wash unit, inspects tubs and stacks for loading onto assigned vehicle for reuse.
  • Operates tub wash sprayer for oversized reusable tubs ensuring the unit is operating properly. Inspect tubs and stacks for loading onto assigned vehicle for reuse.

  • Talking
  • Repetitive Motions
  • Walking
  • Hearing

Field: This job operates in both inside garage, shop or gas plant conditions as well as outside conditions that include inclement weather, heat and humidity.

As part of the ongoing employment requirements, the successful candidate may be subject to drug and alcohol testing—including pre‑employment screening, post‑incident evaluations, reasonable suspicion checks, and random testing—in accordance with government regulations and company policies.

title: Experienced Social Scientist

Build the Future with Us - WSP is seeking an Intermediate Social Scientist to join our BC Ecology and Environmental Impact Assessment team on a full-time basis. Our team of social scientists and engagement specialists work throughout BC and elsewhere in Canada and internationally on environmental and socio-economic impact assessments, environmental permitting, policy and program development, social management planning, sustainability initiatives, community engagement, social due diligence, and third-party monitoring. Through mentorship, hands-on experience, and exposure to a diverse project portfolio, you will strengthen your social science consulting skills while helping shape a sustainable future.

Your Impact

  • Support socio-economic and land and marine use assessments, as part of environmental impact assessments for a wide variety of sectors including infrastructure, power and renewable energy, mining, and oil & gas
  • Support secondary research, primary data collection, and field work, including qualitative and quantitative data collection and information sharing with Indigenous Nations, user groups, communities, and the public
  • Conduct analysis and reporting of socio-economic research
  • Support Indigenous and public engagement activities for projects
  • Assist with development of socio-economic and land and marine use management plans for projects, to meet regulatory and corporate requirements and best practice
  • Support other WSP services as may be required, such as socio-economic monitoring, health impact assessments, permit applications, and social compliance and due diligence reviews
  • Assist senior staff with task coordination and management, proposal development, and technical presentations

The Skills That Set You Apart

  • A university degree (graduate degree preferred) in a social science, natural resource management, or other relevant program
  • Minimum of 3 to 5 years of relevant professional experience
  • Demonstrated social science research skills and experience (e.g., use of government statistics, surveys, interviews, focus groups), including design and implementation of research programs and logistics
  • Strong team player with experience working on multi-disciplinary projects and teams
  • Experience working with Indigenous nations, communities and the public
  • Available for business travel and extended working hours as may be required from time to time
  • Excellent work ethic with strong attention to detail, organization and time management skills
  • Highly effective verbal and written communication skills
  • A strong passion – WSP will give serious consideration to candidates that may not demonstrate all the above qualifications but show promise and a desire to develop their career in this area of practice
  • Commitment to health, safety, quality, and continuous learning, with a proactive approach to problem solving and stakeholder engagement

Why Choose WSP?

  • We exist to shape communities to advance humanity. The brightest engineers, advisors and scientists from across the globe call WSP home

  • Proudly Canadian – we are a Top 100 Employer in Canada for 2026

  • A global community of brilliant minds – your next idea, mentor, or opportunity is always within reach

  • Flexible work, real balance – we recognize the importance of balance in our lives and encourage you to prioritize the balance in yours

#WeAreWSP

Compensation

  • AB, BC, NT, NU, SK & YT: $80,800 to $107,000
  • MB & ON: $73,700 to $101,500
  • NB, NL, NS, PEI & QC: $73,000 to $96,900

Disclosure:
The final salary awarded for this role may vary from the above range based on several factors including, but not limited to, relevant education, qualifications, certifications, experience, skills, seniority, geographic location, performance, and business or organizational needs. The wage range provided in this job posting may be subject to change for business purposes.

Ready to Build Your Future?

Bring your passion for social sciences to a team where your contributions make a measurable impact. At WSP, you'll gain exposure to meaningful projects, collaborate with industry-leading professionals, and develop the skills needed to grow into future technical and leadership opportunities. If you're ready to make your mark and help deliver projects that shape communities across British Columbia, we'd love to hear from you.

title: Associate - Central P&A - Core
description:
About the Role

Do you thrive at the intersection of financial precision, executive storytelling and operational discipline? Our Planning & Analysis team is seeking an Associate to anchor one of the most consequential functions in our finance organization — end-to-end ownership of the monthly close, reporting cycle and CFO-level deliverables.

This is not a passive reporting role. It is a high-visibility, high-accountability seat that directly shapes how senior leadership understands and acts on business performance. You will own the production and governance of core financial reporting outputs — from Business Day close decks and Management Expense Views to Business Unit Reviews, Executive Management Reports and Firmwide commentary submissions. You will serve as the connective tissue between finance partners, business managers and CFO leadership, ensuring every deliverable is accurate, timely, version-controlled and analytically insightful. If you are energized by the rigor of a close cycle and the craft of translating complex financials into compelling executive narratives, this role is built for you.

Candidate Profile

The ideal candidate is a detail-oriented, analytically driven finance professional who combines deep technical fluency with sharp communication skills and disciplined stakeholder management. You understand the mechanics of a monthly close cycle intimately — the sequencing, the pressure points and the material consequences of a missed deadline or an unvalidated figure.

You bring structured thinking to ambiguous situations, a continuous improvement mindset to recurring processes and the professional confidence to challenge data, push back on assumptions and drive consensus across competing stakeholders. Candidates with backgrounds in P&A, FP&A, CFO support, corporate finance, financial reporting, management reporting, business management, consulting or analytics are strongly encouraged to apply.

Job Responsibilities

  • Support the monthly close, budget and planning cycles through the delivery of timely and accurate financial reporting.
  • Prepare and review trend analysis, variance analysis and business commentary to inform decision-making.
  • Produce and maintain MEV self-serve templates; provide reporting guidance and FDI communications to finance and business teams.
  • Validate source data and manage commentary collector processes, encompassing roll-forward preparation, pre-population and submission validation.
  • Own end-to-end CFO Summary preparation, managing all review points and ensuring follow-ups are driven to resolution with rigor and urgency.
  • Prepare Firmwide commentary submissions, synthesizing diverse business narratives into a cohesive, senior-ready view.
  • Partner with P&A, CFO, business management and finance stakeholders to understand variance drivers and evolving reporting requirements.
  • Conduct monthly, quarterly and annual variance analysis, identifying key drivers and delivering meaningful insights to support management decisions.
  • Support ad hoc requests, issue resolution, deep-dive analyses and strategic finance initiatives.
  • Develop presentations and reporting packs for senior management, clearly articulating financial performance, risks and opportunities.
  • Leverage AI and automation tools to drive process improvements and operational efficiencies across reporting and planning cycles.

Required Qualifications, Capabilities, and Skills

  • MBA, CA or postgraduate degree in Finance, Economics, Accounting, Business or a related discipline.
  • 5+ years of relevant experience in Planning & Analysis / FP&A, CFO support, corporate finance, expense management, financial reporting, management reporting, financial research, valuation, banking, financial services, consulting or analytics.
  • Strong familiarity with monthly close and reporting cycles, including Business Day sequencing, variance analysis, commentary production and executive pack preparation.
  • Solid command of financial statements, expense management, budgeting, forecasting and business performance drivers.
  • Advanced Excel and PowerPoint skills — encompassing complex formulas, data validation, version control and executive-ready presentation design.
  • Hands-on experience with Essbase or an equivalent financial reporting and planning platform.
  • Demonstrated ability to distill complex financial data into clear, concise narratives for CFO and senior leadership audiences, both verbally and in writing.
  • Proven ability to manage competing priorities under tight deadlines, sustaining quality and accuracy across multiple simultaneous deliverables.
  • Ability to coordinate input from diverse finance and business partners across geographies and functions, building alignment efficiently.
  • A highly organized, process-disciplined self-starter who applies rigorous controls thinking to recurring financial workflows.

Preferred Qualifications, Capabilities, and Skills

  • Prior experience in banking, financial services or global finance functions, with exposure to Firmwide or line-of-business P&A environments.
  • Hands-on experience with business intelligence and automation platforms — Tableau, Alteryx, Power BI or equivalent.
  • Working knowledge of AI-assisted finance tools and their application to reporting automation, commentary generation and process optimization.

title: Foreman - Underground (Oncor)
description:
Position Summary

The Foreman is a safety focused professional with the ability to lead a crew to construct and repair electrical underground distribution systems. You will work on energized and de‑energized powerlines and may be required to travel to different job sites, including out‑of‑state locations, as operational and customer needs dictate. You will report to the General Foreman.

Essential Functions

  • Perform new construction, maintain and repair energized and de‑energized underground distribution systems while putting safety first.

  • Lead crew members and conduct pre-job and tailgate safety briefings.

  • Must be experienced with coaching and training lower classification employees in safe and productive work procedures.

  • Oversee work related to each project and assume full responsibility for its quality and completion deadline.

  • Install and repair underground facilities, underground conductors, including trouble shooting and fault locating on primary and secondary systems.

  • Comprehensive knowledge of switching and tagging procedures, grounding and induced voltage on energized and de-energized lines while using the proper tools and test equipment.

  • Understand how and when to obtain a one shot on a reclosing device.

  • Work in confined spaces, and in proximity to energized equipment.

  • Operate and maintain excavation equipment to include backhoes, trenchers, excavators, and pulling equipment.

  • Work outdoors in varying environmental conditions, including extreme heat, cold, rain, wind, and inclement weather.

  • Available to work outages, storms, emergencies including on call rotation.

  • Perform live‑line work using approved PPE and insulated sticks required for testing voltage and switching of energized lines.

  • Follow all safety protocols including PPE use and possess a comprehensive understanding of insulated protective cover to isolate differences of potential.

Minimum Requirements

  • Five (5) years of recent underground line experience.

  • Valid Commercial Driver's License (CDL).

  • Willing to travel long distances on short notice.

  • Lift, carry, push, or pull materials and equipment weighing up to 50 pounds.

  • Work for extended periods at job locations, including out‑of‑state assignments.

  • Willing to work outside of normal business hours, including weekends, holidays, emergency callouts, and overtime.

Physical Demands

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to perform the essential functions of this job.

While performing the responsibilities of this job, you will be required to talk, listen and use hand signals to communicate. The job frequently requires you to stand; walk; use hands and fingers to handle objects, operate tools or controls; reach with hands and arms.

Work Environment

While performing the responsibilities of this job, you are frequently exposed to fumes or airborne particles, moving mechanical parts and vibration. You are occasionally exposed to a variety of extreme conditions at construction job sites. The noise level in the work environment and job sites can be loud. You will perform job responsibilities in extreme heat, cold, wet, windy, and storm conditions.

Our Benefits

  • Medical, dental and vision insurance

  • HSA, dependent care and medical flexible spending accounts

  • Employee Assistance Program (EAP)

  • 401(k) with company match

  • Life insurance, and short-term and long-term disability

  • Paid time off, paid holidays, and family and medical leave

If this sounds like you, come join the PIKE family.

About Us

Founded in 1945, Pike is a leading provider of construction, repair and engineering services for electric and gas utilities, as well as telecommunications companies with a growing portfolio of turnkey renewable projects. We work with hundreds of utility clients across the country, and we continuously expand our offerings to supply our customers with the ideas, technology, experience, workforce and equipment to perform any job.

"Essential" is the one word that sums up who we are, the work we do and what our people mean to us. Each of our employees plays a critical role in ensuring that infrastructure systems are up and running when people and businesses need them.

Pike is a family-oriented workplace with a strong culture of safety, collaboration, innovation and exceptional customer service.

Pike Electric LLC, is an equal opportunity employer.
